ABCC8.co_receptor_rationale: SUR1 carries a C-terminal RKR ER-retention signal that is masked only when SUR1 assembles with Kir6.2 (KCNJ11) into the full octameric KATP complex; unassembled SUR1 is retained in the ER and does not reach the plasma membrane (a2_evi_20). TMD0/L0 mutations that disrupt Kir6.2 contact impair trafficking to the surface (a1_evi_04).
ABCC8.surface_specificity_rationale: Surface biotinylation confirms a plasma membrane pool in beta-cells (a2_evi_23), but IHC shows co-distribution in cytoplasm/insulin granules and nuclear membrane (a2_evi_19); GBM lines show both plasmalemmal and mitochondrial pools (a2_evi_14).

ABCC9.co_receptor_rationale: Functional KATP channels require co-assembly of four SUR2 (ABCC9) subunits with four Kir6.x subunits to reach the plasma membrane (a1_evi_02). Surface biotinylation in HEK-293 cells confirmed SUR2A membrane expression only when co-expressed with Kir6.2; the p.S1054Y mutation reduced both SUR2A and Kir6.2 surface levels together (a1_evi_04). SUR2 does not traffic to the surface as a monomer; obligate hetero-octameric assembly is required.
ABCC9.surface_specificity_rationale: Primary compartment is the plasma membrane as part of the KATP channel complex; dual localization to mitochondria is isoform-specific (SUR2A-55 splice variant only, a2_evi_20) and cytosolic redistribution is restricted to high-grade tumor cells (a2_evi_16). The dominant steady-state pool is surface-resident.

ABCG5.co_receptor_rationale: ABCG5 is an obligate half-transporter that must heterodimerize with ABCG8 to form a functional surface-resident complex (a1_evi_18). Multiple sources confirm ABCG5 and ABCG8 are co-localized as a heterodimer at the canalicular membrane (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_06). Cryo-EM structure was solved as the ABCG5/G8 heterodimer (a1_evi_06). No evidence of ABCG5 reaching the surface independently.
ABCG5.surface_specificity_rationale: The canonical localization is the apical plasma membrane of hepatocytes and enterocytes; no significant intracellular-only pool is documented — the protein traffics to the PM as a heterodimer (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_06, a2_evi_06).

ABCG8.co_receptor_rationale: ABCG8 homodimers are retained in the ER and do not reach the plasma membrane; only the ABCG5/ABCG8 heterodimer traffics to the cell surface (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_03). Domain-swap chimera experiments confirm the N-terminal cytosolic domain of ABCG8 carries ER-retention determinants that are relieved only by ABCG5 pairing (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_04).
ABCG8.surface_specificity_rationale: The heterodimer is surface-dominant at the apical membrane of its two expressing cell types, but ABCG8 alone is ER-retained; surface vs. intracellular split is partner-dependent (a2_evi_03, a2_evi_04).

ACHE.co_receptor_rationale: AChE-T requires PRiMA for membrane anchoring at cholinergic synapses in brain (a1_evi_02, a2_evi_02) and ColQ for anchoring at the neuromuscular junction in muscle (a1_evi_03, a2_evi_03). AChE-H is GPI-anchored independently via lipid modification (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_04). Dependency is isoform-specific: T isoform requires a partner anchor protein to reach the surface.
ACHE.surface_specificity_rationale: All three membrane-anchored isoforms (H via GPI, T via PRiMA or ColQ) place the catalytic domain extracellularly; live-cell flow confirms surface dominance in cancer lines (a1_evi_07, a1_evi_09). ER retention occurs only under drug-induced stress (a1_evi_13).

ADAM2.co_receptor_rationale: In calmegin-KO mice, ADAM2 is undetectable in mature sperm due to failed ER heterodimerization with fertilin-α (ADAM1), abolishing surface display (a2_evi_19). ADAM5 KO also reduces ADAM2 levels on sperm surface (a2_evi_20), and Garin3 KO decreases ADAM family membrane protein levels (a2_evi_21). Calmegin is an obligate ER chaperone for ADAM2 surface trafficking; fertilin-α heterodimerization is required for surface delivery.
ADAM2.surface_specificity_rationale: Live-cell surface biotinylation MS (a2_evi_10) and non-permeabilized flow cytometry/IF on intact sperm (a1_evi_16, a1_evi_17, a1_evi_24) confirm the dominant pool is plasma-membrane-anchored on spermatozoa; intracellular ER pool is transient and maturation-dependent (a2_evi_19).

AMIGO2.co_receptor_rationale: a2_evi_20 documents that AMIGO2 surface trafficking and plasma membrane localization are controlled by assembly with Kv2.1 and Kv2.2 voltage-gated potassium channels in heterologous expression systems; all three AMIGO family members require Kv2 co-assembly for proper surface trafficking. This is a trafficking-level dependency, not merely modulatory. Note: this dependency is established in neuronal/heterologous contexts; cancer-cell surface expression (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_04) may reflect Kv2-independent trafficking in non-neuronal cells, but no ledger entry explicitly demonstrates Kv2-independent surface trafficking.
AMIGO2.surface_specificity_rationale: Canonical type I TM topology with large extracellular LRR-Ig domain; surface biotinylation MS confirmed plasma membrane presence (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_04); functions as a surface adhesion receptor and NPTX1 receptor (a1_evi_14, a1_evi_17); no significant intracellular-only pool documented.

AMN.co_receptor_rationale: Multiple primary studies show AMN and cubilin are mutually dependent for surface trafficking: cubilin expressed without AMN is retained in ER/Golgi (a2_evi_15, a1_evi_10); AMN expressed alone can reach the surface (a2_evi_16) but CUBN variants disrupting AMN association cause AMN cytoplasmic mislocalization (a2_evi_25, a1_evi_23). AMN-mediated glycosylation of cubilin is also required for surface expression of the complex (a1_evi_20). The dependency is mutual and obligate for the functional cubam complex.
AMN.surface_specificity_rationale: AMN is the transmembrane anchor of cubam and reaches the plasma membrane in normal absorptive epithelia (a1_evi_09, a1_evi_12), but a significant endosomal pool coexists with the surface pool due to constitutive endocytic cycling (a2_evi_16, a2_evi_18), and disease-state mutations drive complete ER retention (a2_evi_21, a2_evi_22).

ATP12A.co_receptor_rationale: ATP12A is retained in the ER when expressed alone in COS cells; co-expression with a beta-subunit (gastric H,K-ATPase beta or Na,K-ATPase beta1) is required for surface trafficking (a1_evi_23, a2_evi_09). Functional surface expression in HEK293 and Xenopus oocytes is only achieved with beta-subunit co-expression (a1_evi_13, a1_evi_14).
ATP12A.surface_specificity_rationale: In native polarized epithelia, ATP12A localizes constitutively to the apical plasma membrane (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_09, a2_evi_06); intracellular retention occurs only when the beta-subunit is absent (a1_evi_23), a condition not present in endogenous tissues.

ATP1A1.co_receptor_rationale: ATP1A1 is an obligate heterodimer with a beta subunit (ATP1B1/B2/B3) that is essential for plasmalemma localization (a1_evi_03). Without the beta subunit, the alpha subunit does not reach the surface. IHC co-localization of ATP1A1 with ATP1B2 at basolateral membranes of inner ear dark cells corroborates this obligate pairing (a1_evi_06). Beta-subunit epigenetic silencing in hematopoietic cells implies reduced surface ATP1A1 (a2_evi_32).
ATP1A1.surface_specificity_rationale: The canonical localization is the plasma membrane basolateral surface across epithelia (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_05); state-conditional nuclear shift under chronic TNFα (a2_evi_25) and endosomal pool under LAPTM4B overexpression (a2_evi_27) are minor secondary compartments.

ATP1A2.co_receptor_rationale: The NKA α subunit (ATP1A2) requires the β subunit for plasma membrane localization; the αβ heterodimer is the obligatory functional unit (a2_evi_15). Co-expression of unlabeled β subunit was explicitly required to translocate and anchor the α subunit at the PM in HEK-293T cells (a1_evi_08). Without β, α does not reach the surface.
ATP1A2.surface_specificity_rationale: Wild-type ATP1A2 localizes predominantly to the plasma membrane as confirmed by live-cell functional assays (a1_evi_18, a1_evi_19), in vivo proximity biotinylation (a1_evi_10), and PM fractionation (a1_evi_12); intracellular retention is documented only for disease-associated trafficking-deficient variants (a2_evi_12, a2_evi_13).

ATP1A3.co_receptor_rationale: The beta subunit is an obligate trafficking partner for the alpha-3 catalytic subunit: review evidence states the beta subunit 'ensures proper trafficking and localization' of the alpha subunit to the PM (a1_evi_03). Experimentally, co-expression of unlabeled beta subunit was required to translocate and anchor ATP1A3 in the PM in HEK cells (a1_evi_04); without it, ATP1A3 remains cytoplasmic (a1_evi_17).
ATP1A3.surface_specificity_rationale: Dominant pool is plasma membrane in neurons and excitable cells (a1_evi_15, a1_evi_21, a1_evi_10); modest transient ER retention during biosynthesis (a2_evi_18) and cytoplasmic mislocalization only in beta-subunit-deficient or disease-variant contexts (a1_evi_17).

ATP1B1.co_receptor_rationale: ATP1B1 (β1 subunit) acts as an obligate molecular chaperone for the α-subunit: it is required for intracellular transport, functional maturation, and stable integration of the α-subunit into the plasma membrane (a1_evi_24). Without an α-subunit partner, the β1 subunit does not reach the surface as a functional unit. This is an obligate heterodimer for surface delivery.
ATP1B1.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple independent surface biotinylation and KO-validated IHC studies place ATP1B1 predominantly at the plasma membrane; intracellular pools are minor and cell-type-restricted (cochlear marginal cells, a2_evi_26) (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_10, a1_evi_12).

ATP1B2.co_receptor_rationale: ER quality control exports only assembled α–β complexes; unassembled β2 mutants with disrupted α–β association are retained in the ER (high-mannose glycoform accumulation, ER-marker colocalization) and do not reach the plasma membrane (a1_evi_28). MDCK studies confirm equimolar α–β surface stoichiometry gated by ER assembly (a2_evi_33).
ATP1B2.surface_specificity_rationale: Wild-type assembled complex is surface-dominant; surface biotinylation, FACS, and functional assays confirm PM localization (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_07, a1_evi_09). Intracellular pool exists only for unassembled subunits retained in ER (a1_evi_28), not for the native complex.

ATP4B.co_receptor_rationale: ATP4B (beta subunit) must co-assemble with the alpha subunit (ATP4A) to reach the surface: removal of three N-glycan chains from ATP4B inhibits surface delivery of both the beta subunit AND the assembled alpha/beta complex (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_08). Reviews confirm ATP4B stabilizes ATP4A and the two subunits form an obligate heterodimer (a1_evi_16). Surface delivery is thus dependent on alpha/beta co-assembly.
ATP4B.surface_specificity_rationale: In resting parietal cells the dominant pool is intracellular tubulovesicles; surface form appears only upon stimulation-triggered apical trafficking (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_14, a2_evi_07).

BTNL8.co_receptor_rationale: BTNL8 requires co-expression with BTNL3 to form functional surface-displayed heterodimers that engage the Vγ4 TCR. Soluble Vγ4 TCRs stain 293T cells only when BOTH BTNL3 and BTNL8 are co-expressed, not single transductants (a1_evi_11, a2_evi_14). Functional TCR downregulation likewise requires the BTNL3/BTNL8 pair (a1_evi_10, a1_evi_12). ER association of the heterodimer suggests co-assembly during trafficking (a1_evi_15, a2_evi_15). No evidence that BTNL8 alone reaches the surface in a TCR-accessible form.
BTNL8.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple live-cell non-permeabilized assays confirm plasma membrane display as the primary functional localization (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_11, a2_evi_14); ER association is transient during heterodimer assembly (a2_evi_15), not a stable intracellular pool.

CALCRL.co_receptor_rationale: Co-expression of RAMP1, RAMP2, or RAMP3 is required for CALCRL to reach the plasma membrane (a1_evi_02, a2_evi_26). CLR expressed alone in HEK293T cells showed no functional response (a1_evi_03); CLR alone in Xenopus oocytes likewise produced no surface-functional activity (a1_evi_09). Flow cytometry in HEK293 cells confirmed CALCRL cysteine mutants accumulate intracellularly and fail to reach the surface even with RAMP2 co-expression (a2_evi_27).
CALCRL.surface_specificity_rationale: CALCRL is a plasma-membrane GPCR with a documented intracellular pool (cytoplasmic staining in A549 cells, a2_evi_16; intracellular retention of cysteine mutants, a2_evi_27); wild-type receptor traffics to the surface in a RAMP-dependent manner (a2_evi_26, a2_evi_27), yielding a mixed surface/intracellular distribution.

CALHM3.co_receptor_rationale: CALHM3 is consistently described as forming an obligate heteromeric channel with CALHM1; all surface-localization evidence is for the CALHM1/CALHM3 complex (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_04). Palmitoylation-deficient CALHM3 still traffics to the surface (a1_evi_10, a2_evi_15), but no evidence shows CALHM3 reaching the surface independently of CALHM1.
CALHM3.surface_specificity_rationale: Within its expressing cell type, CALHM3 is an integral plasma membrane channel subunit with no documented intracellular pool; surface biotinylation (a1_evi_10) and immunoEM (a1_evi_16) confirm the complex resides at the basolateral PM without significant intracellular retention.

CATSPER1.co_receptor_rationale: Cryo-EM of the CatSpermasome shows CATSPER1 is stabilized at the flagellar membrane within an obligate hetero-complex with CATSPER2-4 and auxiliary subunits CATSPERβ/γ/δ/ε (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_02). Interdependency of protein levels across subunits is documented (a2_evi_01), and CatSper1-null sperm lack channel currents (a1_evi_08), consistent with obligate complex assembly for surface residence.
CATSPER1.surface_specificity_rationale: In spermatozoa, CATSPER1 is a plasma-membrane channel with no documented intracellular pool; cryo-ET and functional assays on non-permeabilized cells confirm surface-dominant localization at the flagellar principal piece (a1_evi_06, a2_evi_09, a1_evi_07).

CATSPER2.co_receptor_rationale: CATSPER2 protein is absent from mature epididymal spermatozoa in CatSper1-null and CatSper-delta-null mice despite testicular expression, demonstrating that the full CatSper complex is required for CATSPER2 to reach the flagellar membrane surface (a2_evi_29). CATSPER2 is a pore-forming subunit of an obligate heterotetrameric complex (a1_evi_02, a1_evi_03).
CATSPER2.surface_specificity_rationale: In spermatozoa, CATSPER2 is an integral flagellar plasma membrane protein with extracellular-facing pore loops; cryo-ET and patch-clamp on intact sperm confirm surface-dominant localization with no documented intracellular pool in mature sperm (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_05, a1_evi_11, a1_evi_12).

CATSPER3.co_receptor_rationale: CATSPER3 is one of four obligate pore-forming subunits of the heterotetrameric CatSper complex (a1_evi_21). Cryo-EM shows auxiliary subunits CATSPERβ/γ/δ/ε each stabilize the complex via direct interactions with pore subunits (a1_evi_03). CATSPERη KO abolishes functional CatSper at the flagellar surface (a1_evi_26). No evidence that CATSPER3 traffics to the flagellar membrane independently of the complex.
CATSPER3.surface_specificity_rationale: Within spermatozoa, CATSPER3 is an integral flagellar plasma membrane channel with no documented intracellular pool; cryo-ET and IF consistently place it at the flagellar surface (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_10, a2_evi_18, a2_evi_19).

CATSPER4.co_receptor_rationale: CATSPERθ (Tmem249) KO abolishes the entire CatSper complex from sperm flagella despite normal testicular expression, demonstrating CATSPER4 cannot reach the flagellar surface without this assembly scaffold (a2_evi_21). CATSPERθ directly scaffolds CATSPER4 during channel assembly (a2_evi_20). CATSPERβ stabilizes the complex via direct interaction with CATSPER4 in the assembled CatSpermasome (a2_evi_19).
CATSPER4.surface_specificity_rationale: In the cell type where CATSPER4 is expressed (mature spermatozoa), it is an integral plasma membrane channel subunit of the flagellar CatSper complex with no documented intracellular pool separate from the assembled flagellar complex (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_02, a2_evi_14).

CATSPERB.co_receptor_rationale: CATSPERB is an obligate subunit of the CatSper holo-complex; its large ECD forms the canopy structure together with CATSPERγ/δ/ε over the pore-forming subunits (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_02). ECD of CATSPERε is essential for holo-complex assembly, implying all canopy subunits including CATSPERB require the complex for proper membrane integration (a2_evi_05).
CATSPERB.surface_specificity_rationale: CATSPERB is a single-pass TM subunit whose large ECD is constitutively oriented extracellularly as part of the sperm flagellar canopy complex; no intracellular-dominant pool is reported (a2_evi_02, a2_evi_03, a2_evi_05).

CATSPERD.co_receptor_rationale: Genetic abrogation of any other CatSper TM subunit causes loss of CATSPERtheta (and by extension CATSPERD) protein in spermatids during spermatogenesis (a2_evi_16). CatSperd-null sperm lack the entire CatSper channel complex (a2_evi_12), and CATSPERD is explicitly required for proper CatSper channel assembly and/or transport to the flagellar membrane (a1_evi_08). Subunits are interdependent for surface presence (a2_evi_03).
CATSPERD.surface_specificity_rationale: CATSPERD is a transmembrane subunit whose entire function is at the sperm flagellar plasma membrane; no intracellular pool or dual-localization is described — the protein is surface-dominant in its sole expression context (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_05, a2_evi_09, a2_evi_10).

CATSPERE.co_receptor_rationale: In CatSper1 and CatSperδ null mice, other CatSper subunits including CATSPERε are absent from epididymal sperm despite testis expression (a2_evi_15), demonstrating that the intact multi-subunit complex is required for stable surface trafficking. CATSPERε cannot reach the sperm flagellar surface without the partner pore-forming subunits.
CATSPERE.surface_specificity_rationale: In its sole expressing cell type (spermatozoa), CATSPERε is stably localized to the flagellar plasma membrane as part of the CatSpermasome complex with no documented intracellular retention pool (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_16, a2_evi_06, a2_evi_08).

CATSPERG.co_receptor_rationale: In CATSPER1-deficient sperm, CATSPERG protein is lost from the flagellar membrane (a1_evi_02, a2_evi_02), and in CatSper1-null mice other CatSper subunits including CATSPERG are absent from epididymal sperm despite testis expression (a2_evi_06). CATSPERG cannot reach/maintain the sperm surface without CATSPER1.
CATSPERG.surface_specificity_rationale: Within its sole expressing cell type (spermatozoa), CATSPERG is a plasma membrane component — cryo-EM places its large ECD on the extracellular face of the flagellar membrane with no documented intracellular pool (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_07, a2_evi_09).

CATSPERH.co_receptor_rationale: Knockout of any other CatSper TM subunit abolishes CATSPERH protein in spermatids (a2_evi_07), and CATSPERH KO removes the entire CatSper complex from flagella (a2_evi_06). CATSPERH scaffolds CATSPER4 for assembly (a1_evi_03). Surface presence is obligately interdependent with the full CatSper complex.
CATSPERH.surface_specificity_rationale: Within spermatozoa, CATSPERH is an integral membrane component of the CatSper complex at the flagellar plasma membrane with no documented intracellular pool separate from the assembly pathway (a1_evi_02, a2_evi_04, a2_evi_05).

CATSPERQ.co_receptor_rationale: KO of any other CatSper TM subunit abolishes CATSPERQ protein in spermatids (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_06), and Catsperq-KO sperm lack the entire CatSper complex from the flagellar membrane (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_05). CATSPERQ cannot reach the flagellar surface without co-assembly with the CatSper complex.
CATSPERQ.surface_specificity_rationale: In mature spermatozoa, CATSPERQ localizes to the flagellar plasma membrane as part of the CatSper complex (a1_evi_09, a2_evi_09, a2_evi_14); no significant intracellular pool is documented in wild-type sperm.

CD180.co_receptor_rationale: Multiple independent sources establish that CD180/RP105 requires complex formation with MD-1 for stable surface expression (a2_evi_24, a1_evi_02). Functional assays show mutant non-glycosylated MD-1 (N96Q/N156Q) reduces de novo surface RP105 delivery (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_28). In CLL, MD-1 RNA downregulation correlates with intracellular CD180 retention despite normal CD180 RNA/protein levels (a1_evi_21, a2_evi_27). Flow cytometry confirms MD-1 expression is tightly associated with CD180 surface positivity (a1_evi_20).
CD180.surface_specificity_rationale: The vast majority of CD180 protein in normal immune cells resides at the plasma membrane; intracellular pools are documented only in surface-negative CLL subsets where MD-1 deficiency impairs trafficking (a1_evi_21, a1_evi_22), not in normal B cells.

CD200R1L.co_receptor_rationale: Mouse CD200RLa/b (orthologs of human CD200R1L) require DAP12 for stable surface expression (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_04). Human CD200R1L carries a charged lysine in its TM segment mediating DAP12 association (a1_evi_02). In HEK293T overexpression, CD200R1L reaches the surface with or without co-transfected DAP12 (a2_evi_02), but the ortholog data establish DAP12 as a required trafficking partner in native myeloid context (a1_evi_01).
CD200R1L.surface_specificity_rationale: Live-cell (non-permeabilized) flow cytometry on primary human neutrophils (a1_evi_10) and transfected HEK293T cells (a1_evi_08) confirms surface-dominant localization; intracellular retention occurs only when DAP12 is absent (a2_evi_03), not under normal myeloid expression conditions.

CD300LB.co_receptor_rationale: DAP12 coupling is mandatory for CD300b/Trem5 surface expression: flow cytometry on BMDCs/BMDMs showed Trem5 (CD300b mouse ortholog) fails to reach the cell surface without DAP12 (a1_evi_09, a2_evi_10). The charged TM lysine mediates this obligate interaction. DAP12 is an intracellular ITAM adaptor that escorts CD300b through the ER to the plasma membrane.
CD300LB.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple independent live-cell non-permeabilized flow cytometry studies and functional ECD-engagement assays consistently place CD300b at the plasma membrane with no intracellular pool reported (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_08, a1_evi_10, a1_evi_11).

CD3D.co_receptor_rationale: CD3D does not reach the surface as a monomer; it assembles obligately into the TCR/CD3 complex. In NK-92 cells (which lack endogenous TCR), surface display of a TCR-like CAR required introduction of the full human CD3 complex (a1_evi_06, a2_evi_05), directly demonstrating that CD3 complex co-assembly is required for surface trafficking.
CD3D.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple non-permeabilized assays confirm CD3D at the plasma membrane of T cells (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_04, a2_evi_01, a2_evi_06); unassembled subunits are transiently ER-retained but the dominant steady-state pool is surface-displayed on mature T cells.

CD3E.co_receptor_rationale: CD3E does not reach the surface as a monomer; it traffics as part of the obligate TCR-CD3 complex. a1_evi_16 and a2_evi_18 directly show that surface expression of a TCR-like CAR construct in NK-92 cells requires the presence of the full human CD3 complex — without it, no surface display occurs. a1_evi_05 confirms all CD3 subunits (γ, δ, ε, ζ, η) are transmembrane components of the same obligate complex.
CD3E.surface_specificity_rationale: Both a surface pool (sCD3, detected by non-permeabilized flow) and a cytoplasmic pool (cyCD3, requiring permeabilization) are explicitly measured as separate analytes in clinical panels (a2_evi_02); the surface pool is the therapeutically relevant fraction.

CD74.co_receptor_rationale: CD74 is the MHC-II invariant chain required for MHC-II complex assembly, trafficking, and peptide loading (a1_evi_01). It functions as an obligate chaperone/escort for MHC-II ER exit and surface delivery; however, CD74 itself also reaches the surface independently as a MIF receptor on multiple cell types (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_07, a1_evi_08). The dependency is modulatory for CD74 surface expression per se — CD74 traffics to the surface on its own as a type II TM protein and MIF receptor, while also escorting MHC-II.
CD74.surface_specificity_rationale: CD74 is surface-dominant on professional APCs (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_08) but maintains a substantial intracellular endosomal pool during MHC-II antigen loading (a2_evi_26) and is predominantly intracellular in non-professional APCs such as mTECs under basal conditions (a2_evi_27).

CD79A.co_receptor_rationale: CRISPR/Cas9 deletion of CD79A in B lymphoma lines causes complete loss of surface IgM and ER retention of BCR components (a2_evi_09, a2_evi_10). CD79A/CD79B heterodimer is obligately required for BCR ER-to-surface trafficking (a2_evi_07). CD79A cannot reach the surface without its heterodimer partner CD79B and mIg.
CD79A.surface_specificity_rationale: CD79A is a canonical plasma membrane BCR complex component; primary compartment is the cell surface on B cells. ER localization occurs only transiently during biosynthesis or under CD79A/CD79B knockout conditions (a2_evi_09, a2_evi_10); no significant intracellular steady-state pool documented in normal B cells.

CD79B.co_receptor_rationale: CD79B (Igβ) forms an obligate disulfide-linked heterodimer with CD79A (Igα) as part of the BCR complex (a1_evi_01). Reconstitution experiments in non-B cell lines (Ba/F3, Sp2/0) require co-expression of CD79A alongside CD79B to achieve surface BCR display (a1_evi_15, a1_evi_17). CD79B first appears on the pre-B cell surface in conjunction with the heavy Ig chain (a2_evi_02), confirming obligate co-assembly for ER exit and surface trafficking.
CD79B.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple non-permeabilized flow cytometry studies confirm CD79B as a constitutive plasma membrane component of the BCR complex across primary B cells and malignancies (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_07, a2_evi_17); only 18% of aggressive lymphoma cases show predominantly intracellular localization (a2_evi_27), making surface the dominant compartment.

CHRNA1.co_receptor_rationale: CHRNA1 is an obligate subunit of the pentameric AChR complex (α1)2β1εδ; it does not reach the surface as a monomer. Only ~30% of synthesized α-subunits assemble into a mature pentamer (a2_evi_24). CRELD1-dependent ER quality control gates surface abundance (a2_evi_25). Rapsyn is required for postsynaptic clustering (a2_evi_20, a1_evi_03). Surface expression requires co-assembly with CHRNB1, CHRND, CHRNE/CHRNG.
CHRNA1.surface_specificity_rationale: Only ~30% of synthesized CHRNA1 alpha-subunits assemble into surface-destined pentamers; the majority is retained in the ER (a2_evi_24, a2_evi_25), with additional endosomal and lysosomal pools under disease or inhibitor conditions (a2_evi_26, a2_evi_30).

CHRNA10.co_receptor_rationale: Mammalian α10 consistently fails to form functional homomeric receptors in heterologous systems without auxiliary factors (a1_evi_20). Surface expression of α9α10 in hair cells requires ligand binding coincident with cholinergic innervation and does not occur in standard recombinant mammalian cell lines (a1_evi_17, a2_evi_11). ACh pre-incubation rescues surface trafficking in HEK293T (a1_evi_06, a2_evi_12). CHRNA9 is the obligate heteromeric partner for productive surface assembly.
CHRNA10.surface_specificity_rationale: Surface-assembled receptor is documented in outer hair cells and ACh-primed heterologous cells (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_06, a1_evi_10); however, without cholinergic priming the subunit is largely retained intracellularly (a2_evi_11, a2_evi_26), and lymphocyte mRNA/protein does not translate to functional surface current (a1_evi_21). Mixed surface/intracellular distribution depending on cell state.

CHRNA2.co_receptor_rationale: CHRNA2 is an obligate subunit of heteromeric pentameric nAChRs; it does not form functional surface receptors alone. Studies co-express CHRNA2 with CHRNB2 or CHRNB4 to achieve surface-expressed functional receptors (a1_evi_08, a2_evi_13). The signal-peptide trafficking study explicitly frames subunit assembly and surface expression as co-dependent processes (a1_evi_06). No evidence in the ledger shows CHRNA2 reaching the surface as a homomeric or monomeric species.
CHRNA2.surface_specificity_rationale: CHRNA2 is a canonical plasma membrane ion channel subunit; its primary compartment is the cell surface as part of pentameric nAChRs (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_05, a2_evi_10). No significant intracellular retention pool is documented beyond ER assembly intermediates.

CHRNA3.co_receptor_rationale: CHRNA3 (α3) does not traffic to the surface as a monomer; it assembles into heteropentamers with CHRNB4 (β4) in the ER before reaching the plasma membrane (a1_evi_04). The fifth accessory subunit (α3 or β4) specifically regulates ER-to-surface trafficking of the assembled pentamer (a1_evi_03, a2_evi_06). Missense mutations in the accessory β4 subunit alter surface localization without affecting assembly, confirming that partner stoichiometry controls surface delivery (a1_evi_14, a2_evi_07).
CHRNA3.surface_specificity_rationale: Direct surface localization is confirmed in neurons (a1_evi_11) and human primary cells (a1_evi_21), but IHC in MCC tumor tissue shows predominantly cytoplasmic/nuclear immunoreactivity (a1_evi_19, a2_evi_18), indicating context-dependent intracellular retention alongside the canonical surface form.

CHRNB1.co_receptor_rationale: CHRNB1 is an obligate subunit of the pentameric muscle-type AChR (α1)2β1δε; it does not traffic to the surface as a monomer. Assembly with α1, δ, and ε is required for ER exit and surface expression (a1_evi_02). The β1 ICD loop alone shows pronounced Golgi retention and rapid internalization when expressed in isolation (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_14), and surface levels of assembled receptor increase only when all subunits are co-expressed (a1_evi_06, a2_evi_15).
CHRNB1.surface_specificity_rationale: In the canonical muscle context, assembled CHRNB1-containing AChR pentamers are concentrated at the plasma membrane postsynaptic face (a2_evi_13); intracellular retention is observed only for the isolated β1 ICD loop, not the assembled pentamer (a2_evi_14).

CHRNB2.co_receptor_rationale: CHRNB2 (β2) only reaches the plasma membrane as part of the assembled α4β2 pentamer; surface biotinylation and anti-ECD immunoprecipitation in SH-EP1 cells show the mature 50 kDa β2 form only when both α4 and β2 are co-expressed (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_05). Chaperones RIC3 and NACHO further enhance surface delivery (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_07, a2_evi_24), and Hsp47 is required for efficient ER folding/trafficking (a2_evi_23). No evidence of β2 reaching the surface as a monomer.
CHRNB2.surface_specificity_rationale: The assembled α4β2 pentamer is the functional form and resides at the plasma membrane; surface biotinylation and live-cell assays confirm the mature receptor is surface-dominant, with only a transient ER-resident immature pool during biogenesis (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_05, a2_evi_22).

CHRNB4.co_receptor_rationale: CHRNB4 (β4) does not traffic to the surface as a monomer; it assembles into pentamers obligately with α3 (CHRNA3). The β4 subunit carries an ER export motif that drives surface delivery only in the context of the assembled (α3)2(β4)3 pentamer (a2_evi_28). The fifth accessory subunit position (α3 or β4) directly regulates ER-to-surface trafficking (a1_evi_03, a2_evi_29). No evidence of β4 reaching the surface as a standalone protein.
CHRNB4.surface_specificity_rationale: Assembled α3β4 pentamers are plasma-membrane-resident ion channels; non-permeabilized IF/immunoEM (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_05) and PM-fractionation MS (a1_evi_12, a1_evi_13) confirm surface dominance; ER pool is a transient biosynthetic intermediate, not a stable intracellular compartment.

CHRND.co_receptor_rationale: CHRND does not reach the surface as a monomer; it requires co-assembly into the pentameric AChR (α1β1εδ or α1β1γδ). a2_evi_26 shows that neither α nor δ fragments alone are surface-expressed in COS cells — transmembrane domains and partner subunits are required for heterodimer formation and surface delivery. a1_evi_23 shows δI58K prevents surface expression of the assembled pentamer. Rapsyn is required for NMJ clustering (a1_evi_07).
CHRND.surface_specificity_rationale: The assembled pentameric AChR containing CHRND is a canonical plasma membrane protein at the NMJ postsynaptic surface; intracellular pools exist transiently during assembly/trafficking (a2_evi_13) but the dominant steady-state localization is the cell surface (a1_evi_08, a1_evi_10).

CHRNE.co_receptor_rationale: CHRNE (epsilon subunit) only reaches the surface as part of the obligate pentameric AChR complex (α1β1δε). Surface expression requires co-assembly of all four subunit types; epsilon alone does not traffic to the plasma membrane. This is documented by the requirement to co-transfect all subunit cDNAs to achieve surface receptor (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_02, a2_evi_06).
CHRNE.surface_specificity_rationale: The CHRNE-containing AChR pentamer is a canonical plasma-membrane ion channel; multiple non-permeabilized assays confirm surface localization with no significant intracellular pool documented under normal conditions (a1_evi_02, a1_evi_05, a1_evi_09).

CHRNG.co_receptor_rationale: CHRNG cannot reach the cell surface independently; all five AChR subunits (CHRNA1, CHRNB1, CHRND, CHRNG) must fully assemble in the ER before membrane insertion (a1_evi_24, a2_evi_14). Loss of CHRNG prevents surface expression of the pentamer (a1_evi_02, a1_evi_03, a2_evi_13). Conversely, loss of any partner subunit equally prevents CHRNG surface delivery.
CHRNG.surface_specificity_rationale: In expressing cells (fetal myofibers, denervated adult muscle), CHRNG-containing AChR is concentrated at the plasma membrane postsynaptic NMJ; ER retention occurs only under loss-of-function mutation conditions (a1_evi_02, a1_evi_03, a2_evi_14, a2_evi_17).

CLCNKA.co_receptor_rationale: Flow cytometry and confocal imaging in Xenopus oocytes showed only a small percentage of ClC-Ka reaches the plasma membrane without barttin (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_16). Coexpression of barttin dramatically enhances surface membrane insertion (a1_evi_02, a2_evi_17). Confocal imaging in MDCK-II/HEK293T confirmed that complete barttin N-terminal deletion retains ClC-Ka in intracellular compartments (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_18). Review-level summary confirms barttin promotes surface insertion (a1_evi_03).
CLCNKA.surface_specificity_rationale: In barttin-expressing renal and inner ear epithelia, ClC-Ka is predominantly at the plasma membrane (basolateral); without barttin only a small intracellular fraction is retained (a2_evi_16, a2_evi_17). Live-cell confocal confirmed sustained PM residence without internalization under pharmacological challenge (a1_evi_10).

CLCNKB.co_receptor_rationale: Barttin (BSND) is required for proper membrane targeting, stabilization, and activation of ClC-Kb; without barttin, ClC-Kb does not efficiently reach the plasma membrane (a1_evi_26). hClC-Kb expressed alone in HEK cells is unstable and undergoes proteasomal degradation (a1_evi_29). Surface biotinylation and confocal imaging confirm barttin co-expression markedly increases membrane trafficking (a1_evi_15, a1_evi_09).
CLCNKB.surface_specificity_rationale: Wild-type ClC-Kb is constitutively at the basolateral plasma membrane in its expressing cells; ER retention is documented only for specific Bartter syndrome loss-of-function mutants (a2_evi_24), not for the wild-type channel (a1_evi_09, a1_evi_13, a2_evi_12).

CNGA1.co_receptor_rationale: In CNGB1-deficient rods, CNGA1 protein is degraded and rod outer segments are almost completely devoid of CNG channels (a2_evi_07). CNGB1 gene therapy restores CNGA1 trafficking to the outer segment membrane (a2_evi_06). CNGA1 cannot reach/persist at the surface without CNGB1 in native rod photoreceptors.
CNGA1.surface_specificity_rationale: In rod photoreceptors, CNGA1 localizes to the outer-segment plasma membrane with no documented intracellular pool in mature cells (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_09); disc-lamellar localization is explicitly ruled out (a1_evi_04).

CNGA4.co_receptor_rationale: FRET with fluorescently tagged subunits directly showed CNGA4 reaches the plasma membrane only as part of the 2:1:1 CNGA2:CNGA4:CNGB1b heterotetramer; when expressed alone, CNGA4 did not self-assemble into surface channels (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_05). C. elegans data further confirm CNG subunit ciliary localization is interdependent (a2_evi_13).
CNGA4.surface_specificity_rationale: Within its expressing cell type (OSNs), CNGA4 is a constitutive component of the ciliary plasma membrane channel complex with no documented intracellular-only pool; surface incorporation is obligate for function (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_05, a2_evi_06).

CNGB1.co_receptor_rationale: CNGB1 requires co-assembly with CNGA1 for outer segment targeting. In CNGB1 KO mice, CNGA1 is degraded and outer segments are devoid of CNG channels (a2_evi_07). Conversely, outer segment delivery of CNGB1 requires preassembly with CNGA1 via the conventional secretory pathway (a2_evi_15). CNGB1 alone does not form functional channels (a2_evi_12).
CNGB1.surface_specificity_rationale: The full-length CNGB1 channel subunit is a bona fide multi-pass TM protein; in rod photoreceptors it is constitutively resident at the outer segment plasma membrane (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_01). The cytoplasmic GARP1/GARP2 isoforms are distinct gene products, not an intracellular pool of the TM subunit (a1_evi_17).

CNGB3.co_receptor_rationale: CNGB3 is an obligate heteromeric subunit of the cone CNG channel; cryo-EM confirms a 3:1 CNGA3:CNGB3 stoichiometry (a1_evi_22). Surface-expression studies in Xenopus oocytes show CNGB3 traffics to the plasma membrane when co-assembled with CNGA3 (a1_evi_14, a2_evi_09). Disease-associated CNGA3 mutations cause intracellular retention of the complex (a2_evi_10), confirming CNGA3 is required for CNGB3 surface delivery.
CNGB3.surface_specificity_rationale: In its canonical cell type (cone photoreceptors), CNGB3 localizes to the outer segment plasma membrane as part of the CNG channel complex; the primary compartment is plasma membrane, with intracellular pools documented only in disease states (a2_evi_05, a2_evi_10) (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_04).

CNTNAP1.co_receptor_rationale: CNTNAP1 forms an obligate cis-complex with Contactin-1 (CNTN1) on the axonal surface; CHO cell transfection shows NF155 binds only cells co-expressing the Caspr-contactin complex, not Caspr alone (a2_evi_03). Disease mutants that fail to traffic to the paranodal surface are retained in the soma (a1_evi_15, a2_evi_16), consistent with contactin-dependent ER exit/trafficking.
CNTNAP1.surface_specificity_rationale: Surface-dominant in myelinated neurons at the paranodal membrane (a1_evi_11, a2_evi_03); primarily intracellular (ER-retained) in brain microvascular endothelial cells (a2_evi_17), and retained in neuronal soma in disease mutants (a2_evi_16) — yielding a mixed profile across cell types.

CYBA.co_receptor_rationale: p22-phox (CYBA) forms a stable heterodimer with NOX2 in the ER; this interaction is required for stability and accurate trafficking of both subunits to the plasma membrane (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_19). Without NOX2, p22-phox undergoes ERAD via Derlin-1 (a1_evi_25, a2_evi_21). Co-expression of both subunits is required for functional surface complex (a1_evi_09).
CYBA.surface_specificity_rationale: PM-surface pool is restricted to phagocytes; in non-phagocytic cells (cardiomyocytes, tumor epithelial cells) the dominant pool is ER/perinuclear (a2_evi_10, a2_evi_14). Even in phagocytes, ER serves as the biosynthetic reservoir before PM trafficking (a2_evi_19).

DUOX1.co_receptor_rationale: ER-to-Golgi transport and PM delivery of DUOX1 require physical interaction with DUOXA1 (a2_evi_01, a1_evi_22). In HEK293 cells, cysteine mutations disrupting DUOX1–DUOXA1 disulfide bonds reduce membrane-surface DUOX1 without affecting synthesis (a1_evi_10, a2_evi_28). In INS-1E beta cells lacking DUOXA1, DUOX1 is retained in the ER and never reaches the PM (a2_evi_06, a1_evi_24). DUOXA1 is an obligate trafficking partner.
DUOX1.surface_specificity_rationale: Apical plasma membrane in DUOXA1-expressing polarized epithelia (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_04), but ER-retained in cell types lacking DUOXA1 such as pancreatic beta cells (a2_evi_06, a1_evi_24); surface fraction is cell-type- and state-dependent.

DUOX2.co_receptor_rationale: DUOX2 requires DUOXA2 for correct apical surface targeting: without DUOXA2, DUOX2 is missorted to the basolateral membrane when paired with DUOXA1 (a1_evi_07, a2_evi_03). Disease mutations disrupting the DUOX2/DUOXA2 complex abolish surface targeting (a1_evi_16). DUOXA2 is an obligate maturation/trafficking partner for apical PM delivery (a1_evi_06, a2_evi_02).
DUOX2.surface_specificity_rationale: DUOX2 is surface-dominant at the apical PM in polarized epithelia (a1_evi_09, a1_evi_25) but also resides in intracellular vesicles in lung epithelial cells (a2_evi_27) and insulin vesicles in beta cells (a1_evi_22), yielding a mixed surface/intracellular distribution across cell types.

FAP.co_receptor_rationale: A rare human FAP variant (Ser363Leu) abolishes FAP dimerization and causes ER retention rather than surface trafficking, demonstrating that proper homodimerization is required for FAP to reach the cell surface (a2_evi_28). Wild-type FAP traffics to the surface as a homodimer; no heterologous partner is required.
FAP.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple independent live-cell flow cytometry studies on non-permeabilized cells confirm FAP is predominantly plasma-membrane-displayed in FAP-expressing cell types (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_08, a1_evi_11); shed/secreted soluble forms exist but the membrane-anchored form is the dominant functional pool.

GABBR1.co_receptor_rationale: GABBR1 carries a C-terminal RSR ER-retention motif that prevents surface trafficking unless GABBR2 masks it via coiled-coil dimerization (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_04). Direct surface-expression assay in HEK293 cells shows Halo-GB1 alone has minimal surface signal; co-transfection with GABBR2 is required for efficient surface expression (a2_evi_29). GABBR2 KO/variant studies confirm loss of GABBR1 surface presence (a2_evi_30, a2_evi_31).
GABBR1.surface_specificity_rationale: The assembled GABBR1/GABBR2 heterodimer is plasma-membrane dominant, but unassembled GABBR1 is retained in the ER/Golgi (a2_evi_27, a2_evi_28, a2_evi_29); the surface fraction is obligatorily dependent on GABBR2 co-expression, making the overall picture mixed.

GABBR2.co_receptor_rationale: GABBR2 requires heterodimerization with GABBR1 for efficient surface delivery: GABBR2's coiled-coil C-terminal domain masks GABBR1's ER retention signal, enabling surface expression of both subunits (a1_evi_17, a1_evi_18). Crystal structure and mutagenesis confirm single-residue disruption of the coiled-coil abolishes GABBR1 surface expression (a1_evi_17). GABBR2 homodimers can reach the surface independently (a2_evi_19), but the obligate heterodimer is the physiological surface form (a1_evi_23, a2_evi_20).
GABBR2.surface_specificity_rationale: Surface biotinylation quantifies 49.6% of total GABBR2 at the plasma membrane under resting conditions (a1_evi_02), with a substantial intracellular pool; the heterodimer assembly requirement means unpartnered GABBR2 can accumulate intracellularly, yielding a mixed surface/intracellular distribution (a1_evi_31, a2_evi_19).

GABRA3.co_receptor_rationale: GABRA3 is an obligate heteropentamer subunit: wild-type alpha-3 alone does not reach the surface; only the A343W gain-of-function mutant enables homomeric surface trafficking (a1_evi_10, a1_evi_11). Native surface expression requires co-assembly with beta (GABRB2/3) and gamma-2 (GABRG2) subunits into the pentameric complex (a2_evi_06, a1_evi_01).
GABRA3.surface_specificity_rationale: As an integral four-pass membrane subunit of a pentameric ion channel, GABRA3 is surface-dominant when expressed; surface biotinylation (a1_evi_08) and functional patch-clamp assays (a1_evi_17, a1_evi_22) confirm the surface-resident pool. No significant intracellular-only pool is documented in the ledger.

GABRA5.co_receptor_rationale: GABRA5 is an obligate subunit of hetero-pentameric GABA-A receptors; it does not form functional surface channels alone. Canonical assembly requires co-expression of β and γ subunits (α2β2γ stoichiometry) for ER exit and surface trafficking (a1_evi_02). Stable cell lines expressing α5β2γ2 confirm surface expression only in the context of the full hetero-pentamer (a1_evi_08).
GABRA5.surface_specificity_rationale: Canonical topology places the receptor at the plasma membrane as an integral multipass complex; membrane fractionation WBs (a1_evi_12, a1_evi_14), synaptosomal preparations (a1_evi_18), and live-cell electrophysiology (a1_evi_19, a1_evi_20) all confirm the dominant pool is surface-resident in neurons and tumor cells.

GABRB1.co_receptor_rationale: Wild-type hbeta1 does NOT form homomeric surface receptors in somatic cells; surface expression requires co-assembly with alpha and gamma/delta subunits into a heteropentamer (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_01). Three ECD residue sets prevent homomeric surface assembly, and only heteromeric complexes reach the plasma membrane (a1_evi_06).
GABRB1.surface_specificity_rationale: In neurons, GABRB1 is canonically a postsynaptic plasma membrane protein within heteropentameric GABA-A receptor complexes (a2_evi_02, a2_evi_17, a2_evi_18). Intracellular retention occurs only when heteromeric assembly partners are absent (a2_evi_01); in native neurons with co-expressed alpha/gamma subunits, the surface form dominates.

GABRB2.co_receptor_rationale: GABRB2 (β2) does not traffic to the surface as a monomer; it assembles into heteropentameric complexes (e.g., α1β2γ2) before ER exit. Glycosylation of Asn-104 is required for efficient α1β2 assembly/stability in the ER (a2_evi_19). γ subunit co-assembly rescues surface delivery of β2-containing receptors that fail as αβ dimers (a2_evi_20). Hsp47 chaperone modulates surface levels (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_16), confirming obligate hetero-assembly for surface delivery.
GABRB2.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple non-permeabilized assays confirm the assembled receptor is plasma-membrane-dominant; ER retention occurs only transiently during assembly or with misfolded variants (a2_evi_19); no significant cytoplasmic or nuclear pool documented (a1_evi_07, a1_evi_05).

GABRB3.co_receptor_rationale: GABRB3 β3 is an obligate subunit of heteropentameric GABA-A receptors; it does not traffic to the surface as a monomer under physiological conditions. Flow cytometry and confocal microscopy show that wild-type β3 supports surface trafficking of partnering γ2 subunits, and mutant β3 reduces γ2 surface levels (a1_evi_09, a2_evi_15). Crystal structure of homomeric β3 (a1_evi_04) shows homomers can form in vitro but native surface expression requires co-assembly with α/γ partners (a2_evi_03).
GABRB3.surface_specificity_rationale: Wild-type β3 is predominantly at the plasma membrane in neurons and heterologous cells under normal conditions (a1_evi_09, a1_evi_07); intracellular retention is documented only for disease-associated variants (a1_evi_12, a2_evi_18), not wild-type.

GABRD.co_receptor_rationale: Live-cell confocal on non-permeabilized N2a cells showed GABRD δ subunit reaches the membrane only when co-expressed with α1 AND β2; expressed alone or with a single partner it remains intracellular (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_03). Native brain receptors assemble as α1/4/6·β2/3·δ pentamers (a1_evi_27); no evidence of independent surface trafficking.
GABRD.surface_specificity_rationale: When properly assembled into the heteropentamer, GABRD is surface-dominant at extrasynaptic plasma membrane domains; intracellular retention occurs only when partner subunits are absent (a2_evi_03, a1_evi_04), not under normal neuronal conditions.

GABRG1.co_receptor_rationale: GABRG1 encodes the γ1 subunit of heteropentameric GABA-A receptors, which obligately assemble as 2α+2β+1γ complexes (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_02). The γ subunit does not traffic to the surface as a monomer; surface expression requires co-assembly with α and β subunits into the pentameric complex (a1_evi_03).
GABRG1.surface_specificity_rationale: As a canonical GABA-A receptor subunit, GABRG1 functions exclusively in the heteropentameric surface complex; the primary compartment is the plasma membrane (a1_evi_03, a2_evi_07); an intracellular astrocytic pool in AD mouse hippocampus is a minor, disease-specific signal (a2_evi_14).

GABRG2.co_receptor_rationale: GABRG2 is an obligate subunit of a pentameric GABA-A receptor; it cannot reach the surface as a monomer. Assembly with α and β subunits is required for ER exit and forward trafficking (a1_evi_23). Hsp47 chaperone modulates surface delivery of assembled receptors (a1_evi_24). Mutant γ2 subunits that fail to assemble are ER-retained (a2_evi_18, a2_evi_20).
GABRG2.surface_specificity_rationale: Wild-type γ2 traffics constitutively to the plasma membrane in neurons (a1_evi_07, a1_evi_08, a1_evi_09); a substantial intracellular ER/Golgi pool awaits trafficking (a2_evi_12, a2_evi_13), and disease-associated variants accumulate intracellularly (a2_evi_15, a2_evi_18, a2_evi_20).

GABRG3.co_receptor_rationale: GABRG3 is an obligate subunit of heteropentameric GABA-A receptor complexes; it does not form homomeric surface channels. Immunopurification of native receptors shows gamma-3 co-purifies exclusively with alpha and beta subunits (a2_evi_09, a2_evi_20). Functional surface expression in heterologous systems requires co-expression with alpha and beta partners (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_06). GABARAP interaction with the gamma intracellular loop modulates trafficking of the assembled complex (a2_evi_18).
GABRG3.surface_specificity_rationale: As a canonical GABA-A receptor subunit, GABRG3 is assembled and trafficked to the plasma membrane as part of the pentameric complex; functional electrophysiology and radioligand binding on intact cells confirm surface-dominant localization (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_11, a1_evi_12). Intracellular pool exists in trafficking vesicles (a2_evi_17, a2_evi_18) but the surface form is the functional steady state.

GABRQ.co_receptor_rationale: GABRQ theta subunit fails to reach the plasma membrane as a homomeric receptor (a1_evi_06, a2_evi_05). Its ICD lacks anterograde trafficking signals; chimeras containing the theta ICD cannot traffic alone but reach the surface when co-expressed with alpha3 or beta3 (a1_evi_07, a2_evi_06). Surface expression is strictly heteromer-dependent.
GABRQ.surface_specificity_rationale: In neurons co-expressing partner subunits, theta reaches the plasma membrane as part of heteropentameric GABAA receptors (a1_evi_07, a2_evi_06); in cells lacking partners it is retained intracellularly (a1_evi_06, a2_evi_05) — a mixed surface/intracellular profile.

GLRB.co_receptor_rationale: Multiple independent experiments show GlyRβ alone does not traffic to the plasma membrane; co-expression with a GlyRα subunit is obligate for surface delivery (a1_evi_14, a2_evi_22). In vivo, GlyRβ is transported together with α1 and gephyrin to synaptic sites (a1_evi_13, a2_evi_23). This is a well-documented obligate heteromeric assembly requirement for ER exit and surface expression.
GLRB.surface_specificity_rationale: In cells co-expressing GlyRα, GLRB is predominantly at the plasma membrane postsynaptic density (a2_evi_19, a2_evi_20); intracellular pool exists only transiently during biosynthetic trafficking (a2_evi_23). Without GlyRα co-expression, GLRB is retained intracellularly (a1_evi_14).

GP1BA.co_receptor_rationale: GPIbα (GP1BA) does not reach the platelet/MK surface independently — it assembles as part of the obligate GPIb-IX-V heterocomplex (GPIbα:GPIbβ:GPIX:GPV in 2:4:2:1 stoichiometry) (a2_evi_01). iPSC-MKs from BSS patients with homozygous GP1BA or GP1BB mutations fail to express the GPIb-IX complex on the cell surface (a1_evi_28, a2_evi_29), confirming obligate partner dependence for surface trafficking.
GP1BA.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple live-cell non-permeabilized flow cytometry studies confirm GPIbα is constitutively plasma-membrane-resident on platelets and megakaryocytes with no intracellular retention pool documented under normal conditions (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_05, a2_evi_04, a2_evi_05).

GP9.co_receptor_rationale: GPIX subunits associate in the ER and mature in the Golgi before translocation to the plasma membrane as part of the GPIb-V-IX complex (a2_evi_07). GP9-KO iPSC platelets show complete absence of GPIX on the membrane surface (a2_evi_12), and GP9 deletion abolishes both GPIX and GPIbα surface expression (a2_evi_13), confirming obligate complex assembly for surface trafficking.
GP9.surface_specificity_rationale: The GPIb-V-IX complex is exclusively expressed on the plasma membrane of resting platelets and megakaryocytes; transient ER/Golgi biosynthetic pools are minor and the steady-state localization is the cell surface (a2_evi_07, a2_evi_03, a1_evi_26).

GRIN1.co_receptor_rationale: GluN1 cannot form functional surface NMDARs alone; it requires obligate co-assembly with GluN2 (or GluN3) subunits for ER exit and surface trafficking. Surface biotinylation shows GluN2B-R519Q retains GluN1-containing complexes in the ER (a1_evi_23). Surface expression studies consistently use GluN1+GluN2 co-transfection (a1_evi_19, a2_evi_28). 14-3-3 trafficking data confirm GluN1 surface delivery requires the heterotetrameric complex (a2_evi_25).
GRIN1.surface_specificity_rationale: GluN1 is surface-dominant in neurons where it constitutively occupies the plasma membrane (a1_evi_12, a1_evi_17), but a significant intracellular pool exists in the ER prior to heterotetrameric assembly and trafficking (a1_evi_23, a2_evi_30); surface vs. intracellular ratio is context-dependent.

HLA-DPB1.co_receptor_rationale: HLA-DPB1 is an obligate heterodimer with HLA-DPA1; both alpha and beta chains are required to form the surface-expressed MHC class II complex (a1_evi_02). K562 cells were co-transduced with HLA-DPA1 and HLA-DPB1 together to achieve surface expression (a1_evi_10, a1_evi_11), and HEK293 transfections used both chains simultaneously (a1_evi_25). Neither chain reaches the surface as a functional monomer.
HLA-DPB1.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple independent live-cell non-permeabilized flow cytometry studies confirm dominant plasma membrane localization on primary human cells (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_07, a1_evi_08); endosomal transit is transient and part of the canonical peptide-loading pathway, not a competing steady-state pool.

HLA-DQA1.co_receptor_rationale: HLA-DQA1 is an obligate heterodimer with HLA-DQB1; neither chain reaches the surface without the other. Cryo-EM of full-length HLA-DQ shows the DQA1/DQB1 heterodimer assembles with invariant chain (CD74/Ii) for ER exit and trafficking (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_04). Surface expression requires co-expression of both chains and Ii chaperone.
HLA-DQA1.surface_specificity_rationale: The canonical steady-state localization is the plasma membrane on APCs; endosomal trafficking occurs transiently during peptide loading but the mature peptide-loaded heterodimer is surface-dominant (a1_evi_07, a2_evi_09, a2_evi_10).

HLA-DQA2.co_receptor_rationale: HLA-DQA2 is the alpha chain of the MHC class II heterodimer; it is non-covalently linked to a beta chain (DQB1 or DQB2) to form the obligate αβ heterodimer that reaches the surface (a1_evi_02). The alpha chain alone does not traffic to the plasma membrane as a functional surface unit — the heterodimer is the surface-expressed entity (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_02).
HLA-DQA2.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple live-cell flow cytometry studies on non-permeabilized primary human APCs confirm plasma membrane as the dominant compartment (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_06, a2_evi_02); ubiquitination-driven lysosomal routing is a regulated turnover pathway, not the dominant steady-state localization (a2_evi_15, a2_evi_17).

HLA-DQB1.co_receptor_rationale: HLA-DQB1 is an obligate heterodimer with HLA-DQA1; neither chain reaches the surface as a monomer. Cryo-EM of full-length DQA1*05:01/DQB1*05:03 confirms the alpha-beta assembly (a1_evi_03). HEK293 OE experiments co-transfect both chains to achieve surface expression (a1_evi_10, a1_evi_12), and allotype-dependent surface levels depend on DQA1 alpha1-domain sequence (a1_evi_12).
HLA-DQB1.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple independent live-cell non-permeabilized flow cytometry studies on primary cells and cell lines confirm plasma membrane as the dominant compartment (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_10, a1_evi_13, a2_evi_02, a2_evi_06); endosomal trafficking is a transient intermediate during antigen loading, not a competing steady-state pool.

HLA-DQB2.co_receptor_rationale: HLA-DQβ2 must heterodimerize with HLA-DQα2 (HLA-DQA2) to form a functional complex, and the heterodimer must associate with invariant chain (CD74/Ii) to reach endosomal compartments and ultimately the cell surface — without Ii, the complex fails to traffic beyond the ER (a2_evi_01). Cryo-EM confirms the obligate trimeric HLA/Ii assembly required for surface delivery (a1_evi_02).
HLA-DQB2.surface_specificity_rationale: Surface is the dominant functional pool on Langerhans cells (a2_evi_02) and B cells (a1_evi_04), but a significant intracellular endosomal pool co-exists in LCs (a2_evi_01), and Ii-associated immature complexes can accumulate at the surface in HIV-infected cells (a2_evi_09).

HLA-DRA.co_receptor_rationale: HLA-DRA is the obligate alpha chain of the HLA-DR heterodimer; it non-covalently associates with HLA-DRB1 beta chain to form the surface complex (a1_evi_01). CRISPR-Cas9 KO of HLA-DRA abolished HLA-DR surface expression entirely (a1_evi_17), confirming that HLA-DRA cannot reach the surface as a functional unit without its HLA-DRB1 partner.
HLA-DRA.surface_specificity_rationale: Dominant plasma membrane pool on APCs confirmed by live-cell flow (a1_evi_09, a1_evi_13); apical cytoplasmic intracellular pool co-exists in polarized airway epithelium (a1_evi_20, a2_evi_04), making the overall picture mixed across cell types.

HLA-DRB1.co_receptor_rationale: HLA-DRB1 is an obligate heterodimer with HLA-DRA; the alpha/beta chain complex is required for ER exit and stable surface expression — neither chain reaches the plasma membrane as a monomer. This is canonical MHC class II biology documented in the pathway enrichment context (a2_evi_24) and consistent with all surface-expression evidence showing the DR complex on APCs (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_01).
HLA-DRB1.surface_specificity_rationale: Primary compartment is the plasma membrane on APCs; ER/endosomal pools are transient trafficking intermediates en route to the surface (a2_evi_24), not a dominant intracellular steady-state fraction.

HLA-DRB3.co_receptor_rationale: HLA-DRB3 forms an obligate heterodimer with HLA-DRA; neither chain reaches the surface independently. Cryo-EM confirms the DRA/DRB trimeric assembly with Ii (a1_evi_01). CRISPR deletion of DRB3*02:02 in Raji cells abolishes surface HLA-DR signal by flow cytometry (a2_evi_18, a2_evi_06), demonstrating DRB3 is required for surface display of the complex.
HLA-DRB3.surface_specificity_rationale: Live-cell non-permeabilized flow cytometry across multiple primary cell types and CRISPR-KO controls confirms the dominant pool is plasma-membrane-resident (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_09, a1_evi_17); minor EV-associated fraction in melanoma is not a competing intracellular pool (a2_evi_16).

HLA-DRB4.co_receptor_rationale: HLA-DRB4 is an obligate heterodimer with HLA-DRA; neither chain reaches the surface alone (a1_evi_05). Invariant chain (CD74/Ii) is required for ER exit and proper trafficking of the HLA-DR complex, as shown by cryo-EM of the trimeric Ii/DRA/DRB assembly (a1_evi_05) and CIITA-driven co-induction of CD74 alongside HLA-DR (a2_evi_21).
HLA-DRB4.surface_specificity_rationale: Primary compartment is plasma membrane on professional APCs; live-cell flow without permeabilization directly detects surface HLA-DRB4 on monocytes, B cells, and T cells (a2_evi_01, a2_evi_03); intracellular pool exists during ER/endosomal trafficking but surface is the dominant steady-state location in APCs (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_19).

HLA-DRB5.co_receptor_rationale: HLA-DRB5 is an obligate beta chain that must heterodimerize with HLA-DRA to form the MHC class II complex; cryo-EM of full-length HLA-DR confirms the DRA/DRB heterodimer as the membrane-resident unit (a1_evi_01). The DRB chain does not traffic to the surface independently — surface expression requires the alpha chain partner (a1_evi_15).
HLA-DRB5.surface_specificity_rationale: Canonical plasma membrane protein on APCs; live-cell non-permeabilized flow confirms surface-dominant localization on professional APCs and inducible surface expression on non-professional APCs (a1_evi_09, a1_evi_10, a1_evi_14).

HTR3C.co_receptor_rationale: HTR3C alone cannot form functional surface receptors; co-expression with HTR3A is required for functional heteromeric complexes at the plasma membrane (a1_evi_10, a2_evi_16). TIRF microscopy confirms AC heteromers at the cell surface only when both subunits are co-expressed (a1_evi_12, a2_evi_15). HTR3C also interacts with chaperone RIC-3 in the ER prior to trafficking (a1_evi_13, a2_evi_17).
HTR3C.surface_specificity_rationale: The plasma membrane is the functional destination for HTR3A/C heteromers (a1_evi_12, a2_evi_15), but a proportion of HTR3C is retained in the ER via RIC-3 interaction (a2_evi_17), making the surface/intracellular split mixed rather than surface-dominant.

HTR3D.co_receptor_rationale: HTR3D alone cannot form functional homomeric receptors and is retained in the ER without an assembly partner (a1_evi_11, a2_evi_13). Co-expression with HTR3A produces functional heteromeric 5-HT3A/D complexes with increased surface expression (a1_evi_11, a2_evi_13). ER co-localization with RIC-3 chaperone when expressed alone further supports intracellular retention without HTR3A (a1_evi_12, a2_evi_12).
HTR3D.surface_specificity_rationale: HTR3D reaches the plasma membrane as part of heteromeric 5-HT3A/D complexes (a1_evi_11, a2_evi_13) but is retained in the ER when expressed without HTR3A (a1_evi_12, a2_evi_12); surface vs. intracellular distribution is assembly-state dependent.

HTR3E.co_receptor_rationale: HTR3E alone cannot form functional receptors or reach the surface independently; co-expression with HTR3A is required to produce functional heteromeric complexes with confirmed surface expression (a1_evi_12, a2_evi_16). IF/IP studies confirm co-assembly with HTR3A (a1_evi_13). RIC-3 chaperone co-localizes with HTR3E in the ER during trafficking (a1_evi_11, a2_evi_17), but HTR3A is the obligate surface-expression partner.
HTR3E.surface_specificity_rationale: HTR3E reaches the plasma membrane as part of HTR3A-containing heteromeric pentamers (a1_evi_12), but a fraction localizes to the mitochondrial inner membrane in transfected cells (a2_evi_14) and to the ER during biogenesis (a2_evi_17), yielding a mixed surface/intracellular distribution.

ITGA2B.co_receptor_rationale: ITGA2B and ITGB3 (GPIIIa) are obligate heterodimers: CRISPR knockout of ITGA2B in iPSC-derived MKs caused complete loss of GPIIb surface expression and a significant reduction in GPIIIa surface levels, with residual GPIIIa rescued only by αV forming αVβ3 (a1_evi_03). Neither subunit reaches the surface without the other; this is an obligate heterodimeric trafficking requirement (a2_evi_01).
ITGA2B.surface_specificity_rationale: In platelets and mature megakaryocytes, ITGA2B is overwhelmingly plasma-membrane-resident; non-permeabilized flow cytometry on intact platelets and iPSC-derived MKs consistently detects robust surface signal (a1_evi_02, a1_evi_05, a1_evi_06, a1_evi_10). The intracellular pool is significant only in neutrophils, which are not the primary expressing lineage (a2_evi_07).

ITGA4.co_receptor_rationale: ITGA4 is an obligate alpha subunit that must heterodimerize with a beta subunit (ITGB1 or ITGB7) to reach the cell surface — integrins are alpha/beta heterodimers by definition (a1_evi_02). On human plasma cells, ITGB1 preferentially pairs with ITGA4 at steady state, preventing ITGA4-ITGB7 pairing, a species-specific pattern (a2_evi_07). Surface LPAM-1 (ITGA4/ITGB7) and VLA-4 (ITGA4/ITGB1) are detected as heterodimeric complexes on B cell subsets (a1_evi_13).
ITGA4.surface_specificity_rationale: Canonical plasma membrane localization confirmed by multiple non-permeabilized live-cell flow studies across diverse primary human cell types (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_07, a1_evi_13); nuclear localization in 3D spheroid models (a1_evi_30) is a weak, context-specific finding that does not displace the dominant surface pool.

ITGAD.co_receptor_rationale: CD11d (ITGAD) does not reach the plasma membrane without CD18 (ITGB2): in heterologous cell lines lacking CD18, CD11d-YFP is retained in the TGN; co-expression of CD18-mRFP relieves retention and allows surface localization (a1_evi_29, a2_evi_20, a2_evi_21). Review confirms no β2-integrin α subunit reaches the surface without its β partner under physiologic conditions (a1_evi_02).
ITGAD.surface_specificity_rationale: Dominant surface pool on leukocytes confirmed by live-cell flow (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_14, a1_evi_17), but a significant intracellular pool exists in THP-1 monocytes (surface vs. total mismatch) (a1_evi_16) and preformed intracellular stores are documented in eosinophils (a2_evi_23).

ITGAE.co_receptor_rationale: αE (ITGAE/CD103) obligately heterodimerizes with β7 (ITGB7) to form the αEβ7 integrin complex; the protein is consistently described as requiring this partner for surface expression and function (a1_evi_03). CHO cells were co-transfected with both ITGAE and ITGB7 constructs to generate surface CD103 (a1_evi_18), consistent with obligate heterodimer requirement for surface trafficking.
ITGAE.surface_specificity_rationale: Predominantly plasma membrane in lymphocytes confirmed by multiple non-permeabilized flow cytometry and IHC studies (a1_evi_08, a1_evi_11, a1_evi_21, a1_evi_26); endosomal localization is a secondary, cell-type-specific phenomenon restricted to dendritic cells (a2_evi_32, a2_evi_33).

ITGAL.co_receptor_rationale: Confocal microscopy on HEK293T cells showed that single-transfection of porcine cd11a alone produced no membrane detection; only cotransfection with cd18 (ITGB2) yielded surface localization (a1_evi_14). Stable HEK293F clones required sequential ITGAL+ITGB2 cotransfection for 98.9% double-positive surface display (a1_evi_16). Biallelic ITGAL LOF in humans abolishes LFA-1 from the leukocyte surface entirely (a1_evi_22).
ITGAL.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple non-permeabilized flow cytometry studies across leukocyte subtypes place ITGAL at the plasma membrane as the dominant pool (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_27, a2_evi_29); intracellular recycling pools in NK cells and neutrophils are minor and mobilization-dependent (a2_evi_26, a2_evi_27).

ITGAM.co_receptor_rationale: ITGAM (CD11b) is an obligate heterodimer with ITGB2 (CD18); the functional surface complex is αMβ2 (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_03). Flow cytometry in single-KO mice showed CD11b+ cells can appear without CD18 and vice versa (a1_evi_12), suggesting some independent trafficking, but canonical surface expression as Mac-1 requires ITGB2 co-assembly (a1_evi_03). Evidence basis is mixed: structural/review plus KO data.
ITGAM.surface_specificity_rationale: ITGAM is a canonical plasma membrane protein on myeloid cells; the dominant steady-state pool is at the cell surface, with a secondary intracellular reservoir in neutrophil granules that is mobilized upon activation (a2_evi_09, a1_evi_21). Non-permeabilized flow cytometry consistently detects high surface signal without permeabilization (a1_evi_07, a1_evi_10, a1_evi_26).

ITGAV.co_receptor_rationale: ITGAV is an obligate heterodimer: it must pair with a β subunit (β1, β3, β5, β6, or β8) to reach the cell surface as a functional receptor (a1_evi_01). Biallelic ITGAV variants cause mistargeting of the integrin, confirming that correct assembly and trafficking to the surface requires the heterodimeric context (a1_evi_24). No evidence in the ledger supports ITGAV surface trafficking as a monomer.
ITGAV.surface_specificity_rationale: Canonical topology is single-pass Type I with a 965-residue extracellular domain; live-cell non-permeabilized flow and functional surface assays consistently detect ITGAV at the plasma membrane (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_13, a1_evi_20); nuclear localization is restricted to HCC with γ-secretase cleavage (a2_evi_27) and 3D spheroid conditions (a1_evi_27).

ITGAX.co_receptor_rationale: ITGAX (CD11c) is a β2-integrin that forms an obligate heterodimer with ITGB2 (CD18); the α/β subunit pairing is required for ER exit and surface trafficking of both chains. The ledger documents ITGAX/ITGB2 as a functional signaling unit on the cell surface (a1_evi_09, a2_evi_25) and describes β2-integrins as heterodimeric transmembrane proteins (a2_evi_03), consistent with obligate heterodimerization for surface display.
ITGAX.surface_specificity_rationale: Live-cell, non-permeabilized flow cytometry consistently detects CD11c at the surface of DCs, macrophages, and B cells (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_02, a2_evi_06, a2_evi_17); intracellular localization is documented only in neutrophils (a2_evi_29), a lineage-specific exception rather than a general pattern.

ITGB1.co_receptor_rationale: ITGB1 is an obligate heterodimer: it requires pairing with an alpha-integrin subunit for ER exit and surface trafficking. a1_evi_24 explicitly documents that endogenous ITGB1 competes with fusion-protein for alpha-subunit pairing, causing ER retention when pairing fails. a1_evi_01 confirms the heterodimeric architecture. Surface expression is contingent on alpha-subunit co-expression.
ITGB1.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple non-permeabilized and live-cell assays confirm ITGB1 is predominantly at the plasma membrane under basal conditions; surface pool is selectively regulated (depleted by AMPK activation without change in total protein) confirming surface-dominant steady state (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_06, a1_evi_26).

ITGB3.co_receptor_rationale: ITGB3 requires an α-subunit partner (αIIb or αV) to reach the cell surface as an obligate heterodimer. In GPIIb-deficient MKs, surface GPIIIa is significantly reduced; residual surface ITGB3 is rescued by αV forming αVβ3 (a2_evi_11). ITGB3-/- MK rescue with WT ITGB3 restores αIIbβ3 surface levels (a2_evi_30). Neither α-subunit alone is sufficient; ITGB3 cannot traffic independently.
ITGB3.surface_specificity_rationale: Canonical plasma membrane localization confirmed by multiple non-permeabilized flow cytometry studies (a1_evi_07, a1_evi_15, a1_evi_16); no significant intracellular-only pool documented in the evidence.

KCND2.co_receptor_rationale: Without KChIP co-expression, Kv4.2 is retained at the Golgi and fails to reach the plasma membrane in HeLa cells (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_19). KChIP1 co-expression drives robust PM redistribution (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_06, a2_evi_20). KChIPs interact with Kv4 N/C-termini at the ER to facilitate tetrameric assembly and PM trafficking (a1_evi_24, a2_evi_21). DPP6/DPP10 co-expression supports functional surface delivery (a1_evi_03).
KCND2.surface_specificity_rationale: In native neurons with KChIP co-expression, Kv4.2 is surface-dominant at the somatodendritic PM (a1_evi_20, a2_evi_07); without KChIP, it is retained intracellularly at the Golgi (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_19), making surface specificity context-dependent.

KCNG2.co_receptor_rationale: KCNG2 (Kv6.2) is a KvS silent subunit that cannot form functional homomeric channels and is ER-retained without a Kv2 partner (a1_evi_02). Surface expression occurs only via heterotetrameric co-assembly with Kv2.1/Kv2.2 (a1_evi_01). Functional patch-clamp in CHO cells confirms surface trafficking requires Kv2.1 co-expression (a1_evi_04). Disease variant disrupting Kv2.1 binding impairs channel function (a2_evi_03).
KCNG2.surface_specificity_rationale: KCNG2 is ER-retained without Kv2 partners (a1_evi_02) but reaches the plasma membrane as a Kv2/KvS heterotetramer in Kv2-expressing cells (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_04); surface fraction is strictly partner-dependent.

KCNG4.co_receptor_rationale: KCNG4 is an obligate silent subunit that cannot form homotetramers and is ER-retained without Kv2 co-assembly (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_03). Kv2.1 KO severely reduces Kv6.4 clustering at ER-PM junctions in native motoneurons (a2_evi_14), and Kv2.1 S590A knock-in abolishes Kv6.4 surface localization (a2_evi_13). Tetramer assembly failure (not trafficking per se) prevents PM expression (a1_evi_08, a2_evi_20).
KCNG4.surface_specificity_rationale: In Kv2-expressing neural subtypes, Kv6.4 reaches the plasma membrane as part of heteromeric complexes (a1_evi_09, a2_evi_12); in all other contexts it is ER-retained (a2_evi_16, a2_evi_17), making surface vs. intracellular distribution cell-type-dependent.

KCNJ11.co_receptor_rationale: Kir6.2 carries a C-terminal RKR ER-retention sequence that prevents plasma-membrane trafficking unless masked by SUR co-assembly (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_05). Multiple surface-biotinylation studies confirm surface expression only in cells co-expressing a SUR subunit (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_09, a1_evi_10). Review explicitly states Kir6 cannot express at the membrane without SUR interaction (a2_evi_24).
KCNJ11.surface_specificity_rationale: Dominant pool is plasma membrane in primary tissues (a2_evi_06, a2_evi_23), but dual localization to mitochondria (a2_evi_11) and rough ER (a2_evi_10) is documented in brain; intracellular pools are constitutive, not solely biosynthetic intermediates.

KCNJ3.co_receptor_rationale: GIRK1 (KCNJ3) requires association with GIRK4 (KCNJ5) for cell surface localization: without GIRK4, GIRK1 homomultimers remain core-glycosylated/non-glycosylated intracellularly (a2_evi_25). GIRK4 KO atrial myocytes show GIRK1 trapped intracellularly, not maturely glycosylated (a2_evi_26). GIRK1 alone can reach Golgi but not plasma membrane without a trafficking partner (a2_evi_28). GIRK1/GIRK2 (KCNJ6) complex stabilizes en route to/in Golgi (a2_evi_29).
KCNJ3.surface_specificity_rationale: Surface-dominant in neurons and cardiac atrial myocytes when partner subunits are present (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_19); predominantly ER-retained in MCF-7 overexpression and in GIRK4-KO cardiac cells (a2_evi_26, a2_evi_27), making the overall picture mixed.

KCNJ8.co_receptor_rationale: Kir6.1 carries a C-terminal RKR ER-retention sequence that prevents plasma-membrane trafficking unless co-assembled with a SUR subunit, which masks the motif (a1_evi_03, a2_evi_07). Pharmacochaperone rescue experiments confirm that surface expression requires the Kir6.1/SUR complex (a1_evi_17). Functional surface expression in native cells is always observed in the context of SUR co-expression.
KCNJ8.surface_specificity_rationale: Plasma membrane is the primary functional compartment (a1_evi_07, a1_evi_19, a2_evi_05), but substantial intracellular pools exist at mitochondrial inner membrane (a2_evi_08, a2_evi_09) and ER (a2_evi_11), and tumor cells show cytosolic redistribution (a2_evi_30).

KCNV2.co_receptor_rationale: Kv8.2 is a 'silent' KvS subunit that cannot form functional homomeric channels (a1_evi_02). In Kv2.1-KO retinas, Kcnv2 mRNA is present but Kv8.2 protein is completely absent from inner segments, demonstrating obligate dependence on Kv2.1 for surface trafficking (a1_evi_08, a2_evi_07, a2_evi_08). Disease mutants also fail to interact with Kv2.1, preventing surface assembly (a1_evi_16).
KCNV2.surface_specificity_rationale: In photoreceptors, Kv8.2 is surface-dominant at the inner segment plasma membrane as part of the Kv2.1/Kv8.2 heteromeric complex (a1_evi_11, a2_evi_12); however, in human retinal organoids a diffuse intracellular/ONL pool is also present alongside the surface-assembled fraction (a1_evi_09, a1_evi_10), indicating a mixed surface/intracellular distribution.

KLRC1.co_receptor_rationale: NKG2A (KLRC1) obligately heterodimerizes with CD94 to reach the cell surface; the receptor is described as a 'dimeric NKG2A/CD94 inhibitory transmembrane receptor' (a1_evi_01) and co-expression of both subunits is required for surface display on reporter cells devoid of the receptor (a1_evi_19). Crystal structure confirms the heterodimeric ECD complex (a1_evi_02). No evidence of NKG2A surface expression without CD94.
KLRC1.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple independent live-cell non-permeabilized flow cytometry studies on primary human NK and T cells confirm plasma membrane as the dominant pool (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_11); an intracellular pool exists only in CD94− γδ T cells prior to activation (a2_evi_32), not in the major NK cell populations.

KLRC2.co_receptor_rationale: NKG2C (KLRC2) is a type II transmembrane C-type lectin that forms an obligate disulfide-linked heterodimer with CD94 (KLRD1) on the NK cell surface (a1_evi_01). All NKG2x family members heterodimerize with CD94 for surface expression (a1_evi_01). The CD94/NKG2C complex is the functional surface unit coupled to DAP12 (a1_evi_05). No evidence in the ledger supports NKG2C reaching the surface independently of CD94.
KLRC2.surface_specificity_rationale: All direct evidence places NKG2C at the plasma membrane as a constitutively surface-expressed receptor on NK and T cells; no intracellular pool or endomembrane residence is documented in the ledger (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_12, a1_evi_16, a2_evi_04).

KLRD1.co_receptor_rationale: KLRD1/CD94 is a C-type lectin that obligatorily heterodimerizes with NKG2 family members (NKG2A/KLRC1 or NKG2C/KLRC2) to form functional surface receptors (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_16). All surface-expression evidence shows CD94 exclusively in heterodimeric form; no evidence of independent CD94 surface trafficking without an NKG2 partner exists in the ledger.
KLRD1.surface_specificity_rationale: All primary evidence places KLRD1 at the plasma membrane on live, non-permeabilized cells; no intracellular pool or dual-localization evidence exists in the ledger (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_04, a1_evi_13).

KLRK1.co_receptor_rationale: NKG2D forms homodimers that gain stable surface expression through assembly with four chains of the signaling adaptor DAP10 (a1_evi_30, a2_evi_03). HEK293 cells stably expressing full-length NKG2D require co-expression of DAP10 for surface presentation in the cell-based binding assay (a1_evi_19). DAP10 is an obligate trafficking/stabilization partner for surface-competent NKG2D.
KLRK1.surface_specificity_rationale: All evidence places NKG2D at the plasma membrane; no intracellular-only pool is documented in non-permeabilized assays, and super-resolution microscopy confirms plasma membrane nanoclusters in resting NK cells (a1_evi_18, a2_evi_04).

LHFPL5.co_receptor_rationale: LHFPL5 requires PCDH15 to traffic to the plasma membrane in heterologous cells and to reach stereocilia tips in native hair cells (a1_evi_08, a2_evi_12). ECL1 of LHFPL5 contains an ER-retention signal that is masked by PCDH15 binding; without PCDH15, LHFPL5 is retained in the ER and fails to reach the surface (a1_evi_09, a2_evi_13).
