LHFPL5.surface_specificity_rationale: In native hair cells, LHFPL5 localizes predominantly to the stereociliary plasma membrane (a1_evi_03, a2_evi_06); an ER pool exists only transiently when PCDH15 is absent (a2_evi_13), and a minor somatic cytoplasmic pool is detected by single-molecule pulldown (a2_evi_16), but the functional form is surface-dominant.

LILRA4.co_receptor_rationale: ILT7/LILRA4 surface expression on pDCs requires association with the FcεRIγ (FCER1G) adaptor molecule; without it, LILRA4 does not reach the cell surface (a2_evi_08, a1_evi_17). This is an obligate trafficking/signalling-complex requirement for surface localization, not merely modulatory.
LILRA4.surface_specificity_rationale: All direct protein-level evidence places LILRA4 at the plasma membrane of live, non-permeabilized primary pDCs; no intracellular pool is documented under resting conditions, and internalization occurs only upon maturation/activation (a1_evi_17, a2_evi_08, a2_evi_09).

LRRC52.co_receptor_rationale: LRRC52 protein is completely absent from Slo3(-/-) sperm and markedly diminished from Slo3(-/-) testis (a1_evi_14, a2_evi_01), demonstrating that Slo3 co-expression is obligate for LRRC52 surface presence in sperm. In cochlear IHCs, LRRC52 protein is absent from BKα-knockout mice (a1_evi_11, a2_evi_08), indicating BKα-dependent surface trafficking in that tissue.
LRRC52.surface_specificity_rationale: In its expressing tissues, LRRC52 is incorporated into the plasma membrane KSper/BK channel complex; no significant intracellular pool is documented — surface biotinylation and functional patch-clamp on intact cells confirm the dominant localization is the cell surface (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_08, a2_evi_11).

MC2R.co_receptor_rationale: MRAP1 is obligately required for MC2R trafficking from the ER to the plasma membrane; without MRAP1, MC2R is retained intracellularly (a2_evi_05). Specific TM4/EC2/TM5 residues mediate this MRAP1-dependent trafficking (a2_evi_07). Co-expression of MC2R+MRAP confers surface ACTH responsiveness (a2_evi_03).
MC2R.surface_specificity_rationale: In MRAP1-expressing adrenal cells MC2R is surface-dominant; in all other cell types lacking MRAP1 it is ER-retained and intracellular (a2_evi_05, a2_evi_06), making the overall picture mixed across cell types.

MRAP.co_receptor_rationale: MRAP1 (MRAP) is an essential chaperone required for MC2R transport to the cell surface and ACTH responsiveness in adrenal cells (a2_evi_01). Without MC2R as its obligate trafficking partner, MRAP does not reach the surface in its functional context — the dependency is bidirectional (MRAP escorts MC2R; MC2R anchors MRAP at the surface).
MRAP.surface_specificity_rationale: MRAP1 transits the ER/secretory pathway en route to the plasma membrane (a2_evi_01), implying a mixed intracellular-plus-surface distribution; no direct fractionation data quantify the surface vs. intracellular pool.

NCR2.co_receptor_rationale: DAP12 is required for NKp44 surface expression: lysine-183 in the NKp44 TM domain mediates noncovalent association with DAP12, and all activating properties and surface expression are mediated through this association (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_07). All three NKp44 isoforms require DAP12 for cell surface expression (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_03).
NCR2.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple independent live-cell flow and functional blocking studies on primary human cells confirm NKp44 is a plasma-membrane receptor when expressed; no significant intracellular pool is documented in activated NK cells (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_08, a1_evi_25, a1_evi_26). Pre-activation intracellular retention is a trafficking state, not a competing intracellular pool in the target cell state.

PCDHA8.co_receptor_rationale: Multiple sources confirm Pcdha isoforms (including PCDHA8) require cis-dimer formation with Pcdhβ or Pcdhγ isoforms as carrier proteins to reach the plasma membrane (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_17, a2_evi_02). Wild-type Pcdha4 without carrier proteins fails PM localization in HEK293T cells (a1_evi_06, a2_evi_03). Surface expression is therefore obligately partner-dependent.
PCDHA8.surface_specificity_rationale: In neurons co-expressing Pcdhβ/γ carriers, PCDHA8 reaches the plasma membrane at synaptic junctions (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_04); without carrier proteins, it is retained intracellularly (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_17, a2_evi_02, a2_evi_03), making surface vs. intracellular distribution context-dependent.

PTCRA.co_receptor_rationale: PTCRA (pTα) reaches the surface only as part of the pre-TCR complex with TCRβ and CD3 signaling subunits (a2_evi_02, a2_evi_04). Reconstituted pre-TCR was barely detectable at the surface even at very high expression levels (a2_evi_04), and loss-of-function of PTCRA alone abolishes αβ T cell development (a2_evi_07, a2_evi_11), confirming obligate complex assembly for surface trafficking.
PTCRA.surface_specificity_rationale: The dominant steady-state pool is intracellular (rapid constitutive internalization into endosomes; a2_evi_03, a2_evi_04), with a transient but functionally sufficient surface fraction on DN3 thymocytes and T-ALL blasts (a1_evi_02, a2_evi_15).

PTPRCAP.co_receptor_rationale: CD45 knockout in CEM/Jurkat cells reduces PTPRCAP protein to ~10% of WT levels (a2_evi_12). In CD45-deficient primary human T cells, PTPRCAP is synthesized normally but rapidly degraded; CD45 cDNA rescue restores expression (a2_evi_13). >70% of PTPRCAP molecules are bound to CD45 in a 1:1 complex (a2_evi_12). PTPRCAP does not reach stable surface levels without CD45.
PTPRCAP.surface_specificity_rationale: Review and functional data place PTPRCAP predominantly at the plasma membrane as a CD45 complex partner (a2_evi_09, a1_evi_02); no significant intracellular-only pool is documented under normal lymphocyte conditions.

RHAG.co_receptor_rationale: RHAG KO abolishes surface display of RhD/CE antigens (a2_evi_05, a2_evi_04), and RHAG loss produces the RhNull phenotype (a2_evi_09, a2_evi_10). Conversely, RhD/CE require RHAG to reach the surface — RHAG is the obligate scaffold. RHAG itself is a constitutive membrane resident in the Rh subcomplex (a1_evi_02), but its own surface trafficking depends on the intact complex.
RHAG.surface_specificity_rationale: RHAG is a constitutive integral plasma membrane protein in erythroid cells with no documented intracellular pool; all evidence places it at the erythrocyte surface as part of the Rh macrocomplex (a1_evi_02, a1_evi_03, a2_evi_01).

RHCE.co_receptor_rationale: CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of RHAG in HSPCs abolishes surface display of Rh antigens (including RhCE-encoded C/c/E/e), yielding near-complete RhNull phenotype confirmed by hemagglutination and flow cytometry on intact cells (a1_evi_07, a2_evi_07, a2_evi_08). RHAG is an obligate chaperone/trafficking partner required for RhCE surface expression.
RHCE.surface_specificity_rationale: RhCE is an integral 12-pass transmembrane protein of the erythrocyte plasma membrane with no documented intracellular pool or dual localization; all evidence places it at the cell surface of erythroid cells (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_05, a1_evi_06, a2_evi_08).

RHD.co_receptor_rationale: RHD is a core component of the Rh complex (RhCx = RhAG + RhD) embedded in the RBC membrane (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_10). Genetic KO studies in mice confirm that RhD requires RhAG as an obligate complex partner for stable membrane integration; RHD does not traffic independently to the erythrocyte surface without RhAG.
RHD.surface_specificity_rationale: RHD is a 12-TM integral membrane protein with no documented intracellular pool in erythrocytes; all evidence places it at the plasma membrane as a core RBC membrane complex component (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_02, a2_evi_10).

SCNN1B.co_receptor_rationale: ENaC is an obligate heterotrimer of α (SCNN1A), β (SCNN1B), and γ (SCNN1G) subunits; all three must co-assemble for ER exit and surface trafficking. Surface biotinylation and functional studies consistently measure SCNN1B only as part of the αβγ complex at the apical membrane (a2_evi_06, a1_evi_04). No evidence of SCNN1B reaching the surface as a monomer or without its obligate partners.
SCNN1B.surface_specificity_rationale: The surface pool is real and directly quantified (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_22), but constitutes a minority of total cellular β-ENaC (≥5% surface-biotinylated under maximal stimulation); a substantial intracellular vesicular pool cycles constitutively with the apical membrane (a2_evi_27, a2_evi_30), placing SCNN1B in the mixed category.

SCNN1G.co_receptor_rationale: γENaC (SCNN1G) requires co-assembly with αENaC (SCNN1A) and βENaC (SCNN1B) to traffic through the Golgi and reach the apical surface; γENaC cleavage-site mutants are ubiquitinated only when co-expressed with α- and βENaC, facilitating Golgi trafficking (a1_evi_06). All functional surface-expression studies use the αβγ heterotrimer (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_15).
SCNN1G.surface_specificity_rationale: Surface biotinylation shows only ≥5% of total γENaC at the kidney surface under maximal stimulation (a1_evi_03), with a large intracellular full-length pool constitutively present alongside the surface-cleaved pool (a2_evi_07, a2_evi_29); surface fraction is regulatable but the dominant pool is intracellular at baseline low-aldosterone states (a2_evi_08).

SGCA.co_receptor_rationale: SGCA traffics to the sarcolemma only as part of the tetrameric sarcoglycan complex. In HEK293 cells, SGCB alone shows minimal surface expression; co-expression of SGCA, SGCG, and SGCD is required for robust complex surface localization (a2_evi_11). Review evidence confirms that loss of any single subunit disrupts trafficking of the entire complex (a2_evi_12). Cryo-EM shows the four subunits co-fold for surface assembly (a1_evi_02).
SGCA.surface_specificity_rationale: In healthy striated muscle, SGCA is a constitutive sarcolemmal protein with no documented cytoplasmic or nuclear pool; surface biotinylation MS (a1_evi_06) and non-permeabilized IF (a1_evi_16) confirm surface-dominant localization.

SGCB.co_receptor_rationale: SGCB expressed alone shows minimal cell surface expression by anti-HA IF on intact HEK293 cells (a1_evi_14, a2_evi_16). Co-expression with SGCA, SGCG, SGCD restores robust surface localization (a1_evi_15, a1_evi_25). Beta-delta co-expression is specifically required for ER export (a1_evi_26). KO of SGCB abolishes the entire SGC at the sarcolemma/NMJ (a1_evi_11).
SGCB.surface_specificity_rationale: In mature muscle, SGCB localizes exclusively to the sarcolemma (a2_evi_15); intracellular pool is transient during early myogenesis or when complex partners are absent (a2_evi_15, a2_evi_16), not a steady-state compartment.

SGCD.co_receptor_rationale: Heterologous-cell IF shows SGCB alone yields minimal surface expression; co-expression of SGCA, SGCG, and SGCD is required for robust surface delivery of the full SGC (a1_evi_18, a1_evi_19). Western blot in cardiac tissue confirms SGCB loss destabilizes the entire complex including SGCD (a2_evi_14). Complex-dependent trafficking is obligate.
SGCD.surface_specificity_rationale: In wild-type muscle, SGCD localizes predominantly to the sarcolemma as part of the assembled SGC; intracellular ER retention occurs only in disease-state misfolding mutants (a2_evi_10), not in the wild-type baseline (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_08).

SGCG.co_receptor_rationale: SGCG surface expression is obligately complex-dependent. In HEK293 cells, robust surface expression of the sarcoglycan complex requires co-expression of all four subunits (SGCA, SGCB, SGCG, SGCD) (a2_evi_13). Loss of any single subunit destabilizes and prevents sarcolemmal trafficking of the remaining members (a2_evi_16). SGCG loss in patient muscle abolishes the entire sarcolemmal complex (a1_evi_05).
SGCG.surface_specificity_rationale: In normal muscle, SGCG is constitutively localized to the sarcolemmal surface as part of the sarcoglycan complex with no documented intracellular pool (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_09, a2_evi_10, a2_evi_13).

SIGLEC16.co_receptor_rationale: Siglec-16 reaches the cell surface specifically in the presence of DAP12 adaptor but not FcRγ chain (a1_evi_01). The charged transmembrane domain of SIGLEC16 is predicted to associate with ITAM-encoding adaptors such as DAP12 for surface trafficking (a2_evi_02). No surface expression was documented in the absence of DAP12.
SIGLEC16.surface_specificity_rationale: Canonical type I single-pass topology places the entire ECD on the outer leaflet (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_07); DAP12-dependent surface trafficking confirmed in transfected cells and macrophages (a1_evi_01); no intracellular retention pool documented in the ledger.

SIRPB1.co_receptor_rationale: DAP12/TYROBP complex formation is required for efficient SIRPB1 cell-surface expression in monocytes and DCs (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_02). The charged TM residue of SIRPB1 mediates this obligate interaction; without DAP12, SIRPB1 does not traffic efficiently to the plasma membrane (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_05).
SIRPB1.surface_specificity_rationale: Major SIRPB1 pool resides in plasma membrane fractions of neutrophils (a1_evi_06); constitutive surface expression confirmed by live-cell flow on monocytes/DCs (a1_evi_03) and functional antibody ligation on intact cells across multiple myeloid types (a1_evi_07, a1_evi_09, a1_evi_12).

SLC3A1.co_receptor_rationale: Multiple independent lines show rBAT does not reach the apical surface without a light-chain partner. In MDCK cells, neither rBAT nor b0,+AT reaches the apical surface when expressed alone (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_06). Without b0,+AT, rBAT is rapidly degraded via ERAD (a2_evi_16). In the S3 segment, rBAT partners with SLC7A13/AGT1; rBAT KO eliminates AGT1 from the apical membrane (a1_evi_10, a2_evi_04). Assembly with a light chain in the ER is the obligate gating step for surface delivery (a2_evi_12).
SLC3A1.surface_specificity_rationale: Wild-type rBAT is routed to the apical plasma membrane upon assembly with its light-chain partner; unassembled rBAT is degraded via ERAD rather than accumulating intracellularly (a2_evi_16, a1_evi_05). No significant cytoplasmic or nuclear pool documented for the wild-type protein.

SLC51A.co_receptor_rationale: Co-expression of both OSTα and OSTβ is required for plasma membrane localization; neither subunit alone reaches the cell surface (a2_evi_05). Surface biotinylation in HEK293 cells confirmed that an OSTβ LL/AA mutant eliminated membrane expression of both subunits (a1_evi_06). OSTβ is an obligate trafficking partner for SLC51A surface expression.
SLC51A.surface_specificity_rationale: When both subunits are co-expressed, OSTα localizes predominantly to the basolateral plasma membrane with no documented intracellular retention pool; single-subunit expression causes ER retention (a2_evi_05), but in native co-expressing epithelia the protein is surface-dominant (a2_evi_02, a2_evi_03).

SLC6A18.co_receptor_rationale: Collectrin (TMEM27) is required for functional surface expression of SLC6A18 in kidney proximal tubule in vivo; collectrin-null mice lose XT2 surface activity (a2_evi_02). ACE2 can substitute in Xenopus oocytes (a2_evi_02) and is independently cited as required for membrane targeting (a1_evi_03, a2_evi_09). Multiple review sources confirm this obligate accessory-subunit requirement (a1_evi_02, a2_evi_03).
SLC6A18.surface_specificity_rationale: When collectrin is present, SLC6A18 is targeted to the apical plasma membrane as its primary compartment; intracellular retention occurs only in the absence of the obligate accessory subunit (a2_evi_02, a2_evi_03).

SLC6A19.co_receptor_rationale: In intestine, ACE2 KO completely abolishes B0AT1 from brush-border membranes (a1_evi_09, a2_evi_11); in kidney, collectrin (TMEM27) KO abolishes renal surface expression (a1_evi_10). Xenopus oocyte co-expression of ACE2 or collectrin dramatically increases B0AT1 surface levels (a1_evi_13, a1_evi_14, a2_evi_15). ACE2 P734L variant directly modulates B0AT1 surface abundance (a1_evi_28, a2_evi_29). Tissue-specific obligate chaperone requirement confirmed by IF (a1_evi_11) and functional assays (a2_evi_13).
SLC6A19.surface_specificity_rationale: In its primary expression tissues, B0AT1 is concentrated at the apical plasma membrane with no documented intracellular retention pool under wild-type conditions (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_24, a2_evi_07); disease variants are ER-retained but wild-type protein is surface-dominant.

SLC7A13.co_receptor_rationale: rBAT (SLC3A1) depletion in mice eliminates AGT1 from the renal apical membrane (a1_evi_02, a2_evi_03). Without fusion to a heavy-chain partner, AGT1 does not traffic to the plasma membrane or show transport activity (a1_evi_03, a2_evi_05). rBAT mutations causing ER retention also abolish SLC7A13 surface expression (a2_evi_10). rBAT is the obligate trafficking partner.
SLC7A13.surface_specificity_rationale: In its primary expression tissue (kidney proximal tubule), SLC7A13 localizes to the plasma membrane as part of the rBAT heterodimer (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_02); no significant cytoplasmic or nuclear pool is documented under normal conditions.

TLR6.co_receptor_rationale: gp96 (HSP90B1) is required for TLR6 ER exit and surface expression; without it TLR6 undergoes ER-associated degradation and fails to reach the plasma membrane (a2_evi_03). TLR2 is the obligate signaling heterodimerization partner and TLR6 co-localizes with TLR2 at the plasma membrane of monocytes (a2_evi_01); however, the ledger does not demonstrate that TLR2 absence abolishes TLR6 surface trafficking per se — gp96 is the confirmed obligate trafficking chaperone.
TLR6.surface_specificity_rationale: TLR6 is a canonical plasma membrane receptor; live-cell flow on primary human cells (a1_evi_08, a1_evi_09) and functional surface-blockade assays (a1_evi_19) confirm the dominant pool is surface-resident with no documented intracellular retention under normal conditions.

TMEM47.co_receptor_rationale: In L fibroblasts lacking endogenous E-cadherin, TMEM47 membrane localization requires E-cadherin co-expression; without it, TMEM47 fails to reach the membrane (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_10). In epithelial cells with endogenous E-cadherin, TMEM47 localizes to junctions (a1_evi_04, a2_evi_11). This constitutes an obligate surface-trafficking dependency on E-cadherin in non-epithelial contexts.
TMEM47.surface_specificity_rationale: TMEM47 localizes to lateral PM junctions in polarized epithelial cells (a2_evi_11, a1_evi_06) but is absent from the membrane in non-epithelial cells lacking E-cadherin (a1_evi_05, a2_evi_10) and in adult podocytes (a2_evi_08). A normally intracellular pool can be mobilized to the PM by viral nsP1 (a1_evi_10). Mixed surface/intracellular distribution depending on cell context.

TMIE.co_receptor_rationale: In tmie zebrafish mutants, GFP-tagged Tmc1 and Tmc2b fail to target to the hair bundle (a1_evi_10, a2_evi_16), establishing TMIE's role in MET complex surface delivery. Reciprocally, TMIE requires the complex context: TMC1/2 fail to reach the cell surface in heterologous cells without hair-cell-specific machinery (a1_evi_19, a2_evi_23). LHFPL5, a co-subunit, similarly requires PCDH15 for PM targeting (a1_evi_20), indicating obligate complex assembly for surface delivery.
TMIE.surface_specificity_rationale: In its native hair-cell context, TMIE is a plasma-membrane-resident single-pass protein at stereocilia tips with no documented intracellular steady-state pool under normal conditions (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_12, a2_evi_13); lysosomal accumulation occurs only in loss-of-function mutants (a2_evi_25).

TRA.co_receptor_rationale: TCRα (TRA) requires assembly with CD3 complex subunits (CD3δ/ε/γ/ζ) for ER exit and surface trafficking; without CD3, TCRα is retained intracellularly. Ledger confirms surface TCR complex detection on Jurkat cells (a1_evi_02, a1_evi_03) and functional surface display dependent on CD3 co-expression (a1_evi_06, a2_evi_08). CD8α/β co-receptor dependency for signaling is noted (a1_evi_08) but the obligate CD3 assembly for surface trafficking is the surface-expression axis call.
TRA.surface_specificity_rationale: All evidence places TRA at the plasma membrane as part of the TCR-CD3 complex on live, non-permeabilized T cells (a1_evi_02, a1_evi_03, a1_evi_06); no intracellular-only pool documented in the ledger outside of CD3-deficient assembly intermediates.

TRB.co_receptor_rationale: TCRβ requires assembly with TCRα and CD3 subunits (CD3εδ, CD3εγ, CD3ζζ) to reach the surface as the mature αβTCR complex (a1_evi_20). Flow cytometry in transfected HEK cells showed robust TCRβ surface expression only when the full αβTCR complex was co-expressed; the preTCR (pTα/TCRβ) was barely detectable at the surface even at very high expression levels (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_07).
TRB.surface_specificity_rationale: Live-cell non-permeabilized flow cytometry consistently detects TCRβ at the plasma membrane of mature T cells (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_13); cryo-EM confirms extracellular ECD topology (a1_evi_01). Intracellular pool detected by western blot of lysates (a1_evi_10) reflects biosynthetic/trafficking pool, not a dominant intracellular compartment.

TREM1.co_receptor_rationale: Multiple ledger entries document DAP12 as obligate for TREM-1 surface stabilization. (a1_evi_03) states DAP12 is 'essential for TREM1 cell surface stabilization, clustering, and signal transduction.' (a2_evi_27) states DAP12 'is required for surface expression and signaling by TREM-1.' (a1_evi_15) shows DAP12 KO mice have low TREM1 surface expression, confirming knockout-level evidence.
TREM1.surface_specificity_rationale: Canonical localization is the plasma membrane as confirmed by multiple live-cell non-permeabilized flow cytometry studies (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_08, a1_evi_09, a1_evi_31); intracellular accumulation documented only in NET-stimulated endothelial cells, a non-canonical cell type and state (a1_evi_28).

TREM2.co_receptor_rationale: DAP12-TREM2 receptor complexes are transported through the secretory pathway to the plasma membrane; unassembled DAP12 is retained in the ER/ERGIC, preventing plasma membrane transport of TREM2 (a2_evi_27). The TM lysine K186 forms an electrostatic interaction with DAP12 D50, establishing the obligate TM assembly required for ER exit (a1_evi_04).
TREM2.surface_specificity_rationale: Multiple independent live-cell and nonpermeabilized assays confirm plasma membrane as the dominant compartment (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_08, a2_evi_06, a2_evi_28); intracellular pools are trafficking intermediates or shedding products, not the dominant steady-state localization.

TRPC1.co_receptor_rationale: Two independent lines show TRPC1 PM trafficking requires partners. (a2_evi_27) confocal+patch-clamp: TRPC1 alone forms ER-retained homotetramers; co-expression with TRPC4 or TRPC5 (not TRPC3/6) increases PM-expressed TRPC1. (a1_evi_04) review: heteromerization with TRPC4/5 enables PM trafficking. (a1_evi_05)/(a2_evi_26) surface biotinylation+IF in HeLa: Orai1α is essential for TRPC1 PM location.
TRPC1.surface_specificity_rationale: TRPC1 reaches the plasma membrane in partner-expressing contexts (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_08, a2_evi_23, a2_evi_24) but is ER-retained as a homotetramer without TRPC4/5 or Orai1α (a2_evi_27); surface vs. intracellular distribution is partner- and state-dependent.

UPK1A.co_receptor_rationale: 293T transfection experiments show UPK1A (UPIa) cannot exit the ER alone and reaches the plasma membrane only when it forms a heterodimer with UPII (UPK2) in the ER; pulse-chase coimmunoprecipitation confirmed ER-resident heterodimer formation (a1_evi_13, a2_evi_24). UPIb, by contrast, can traffic independently.
UPK1A.surface_specificity_rationale: Non-permeabilized biotinylation and IF consistently show UPK1A at the apical plasma membrane of umbrella cells (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_10); cytoplasmic signal in thyroid neoplasms (a1_evi_23) reflects ectopic/aberrant context lacking urothelial trafficking partners.

UPK2.co_receptor_rationale: Transfection experiments in 293T cells show that when expressed individually, UPK2 (UPII) cannot exit the ER and only reaches the plasma membrane when forming a heterodimeric complex with UPIa (a2_evi_08). ER-exit and surface delivery are strictly dependent on UPIa co-expression; intracellular retention occurs without it.
UPK2.surface_specificity_rationale: In native urothelium, UPK2 is overwhelmingly surface-dominant: in vivo biotinylation labels it at the apical PM (a1_evi_01), and the intracellular fusiform vesicle pool represents a pre-fusion reservoir rather than a dominant intracellular compartment (a2_evi_01, a2_evi_08).

UPK3A.co_receptor_rationale: 293T transfection experiments show UPK3A (UPIII) is retained in the ER when expressed alone and only exits to the plasma membrane when forming a heterodimeric complex with UPIb (a1_evi_08, a2_evi_16). Pulse-chase coimmunoprecipitation confirmed ER heterodimer formation as the obligate trafficking step.
UPK3A.surface_specificity_rationale: Non-permeabilized surface biotinylation and IF consistently show UPK3A at the apical plasma membrane as the dominant pool in differentiated urothelial cells (a1_evi_04, a1_evi_09, a1_evi_25); intracellular pools exist only as trafficking intermediates (fusiform vesicles, ER retention without UPIb) (a2_evi_16, a2_evi_18).
